read.purpose: Read bytes from an open descriptor into a user buffer.
read.mechanism: `read_internal` constructs a user `uio`, obtains a referenced fileproc and dispatches file operations; the ordinary entry first calls `__pthread_testcancel`, whereas the nocancel entry enters the I/O path directly.

read_nocancel.purpose: Read bytes from an open descriptor into a user buffer.
read_nocancel.mechanism: `read_internal` constructs a user `uio`, obtains a referenced fileproc and dispatches file operations; the ordinary entry first calls `__pthread_testcancel`, whereas the nocancel entry enters the I/O path directly.

write.purpose: Write user bytes through an open descriptor.
write.mechanism: `write_internal` validates access/guard state, builds the `uio` and dispatches the file's write operation; the ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

write_nocancel.purpose: Write user bytes through an open descriptor.
write_nocancel.mechanism: `write_internal` validates access/guard state, builds the `uio` and dispatches the file's write operation; the ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

pread.purpose: Read at an explicit file offset without using the shared descriptor offset as the request position.
pread.mechanism: Both reach `read_internal` with the positional-I/O flag and supplied offset; only the ordinary wrapper performs its initial cancellation test.

pread_nocancel.purpose: Read at an explicit file offset without using the shared descriptor offset as the request position.
pread_nocancel.mechanism: Both reach `read_internal` with the positional-I/O flag and supplied offset; only the ordinary wrapper performs its initial cancellation test.

pwrite.mechanism: Both reach `write_internal` with positional-I/O state; the common file operation performs the transfer and reports partial progress. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

pwrite_nocancel.mechanism: Both reach `write_internal` with positional-I/O state; the common file operation performs the transfer and reports partial progress. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

readv.purpose: Scatter a read across user iovecs.
readv.mechanism: `readv_uio` imports and validates the vector into a `uio`, then follows descriptor read dispatch; the ordinary entry adds a cancellation test.

readv_nocancel.purpose: Scatter a read across user iovecs.
readv_nocancel.mechanism: `readv_uio` imports and validates the vector into a `uio`, then follows descriptor read dispatch; the ordinary entry adds a cancellation test.

writev.purpose: Gather user iovecs into a descriptor write.
writev.mechanism: `writev_uio` imports vector storage and dispatches the resulting `uio`; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation before the common operation.

writev_nocancel.purpose: Gather user iovecs into a descriptor write.
writev_nocancel.mechanism: `writev_uio` imports vector storage and dispatches the resulting `uio`; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation before the common operation.

sys_preadv.mechanism: `readv_uio` receives the explicit offset and positional flag, separating this request from ordinary shared-offset reads; the non-nocancel wrapper tests cancellation.

sys_preadv_nocancel.mechanism: `readv_uio` receives the explicit offset and positional flag, separating this request from ordinary shared-offset reads; the non-nocancel wrapper tests cancellation.

sys_pwritev.mechanism: `writev_uio` receives the supplied offset and positional flag; it shares descriptor validation and transfer machinery with vector writes. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

sys_pwritev_nocancel.mechanism: `writev_uio` receives the supplied offset and positional flag; it shares descriptor validation and transfer machinery with vector writes. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

open.purpose: Resolve a pathname and create an open-file descriptor.
open.mechanism: `openat_internal` performs the common lookup/open path using the current directory; `open` adds a cancellation test. The deeper `open1` path handles vnode access, fileglob/fileproc allocation and publication.

open_nocancel.purpose: Resolve a pathname and create an open-file descriptor.
open_nocancel.mechanism: `openat_internal` performs the common lookup/open path using the current directory; `open` adds a cancellation test. The deeper `open1` path handles vnode access, fileglob/fileproc allocation and publication.

openat.purpose: Open a pathname relative to a directory descriptor or the current directory.
openat.mechanism: `openat_internal` receives `fd`, flags and mode and resolves the pathname with that starting context; the ordinary entry tests cancellation.

openat_nocancel.purpose: Open a pathname relative to a directory descriptor or the current directory.
openat_nocancel.mechanism: `openat_internal` receives `fd`, flags and mode and resolves the pathname with that starting context; the ordinary entry tests cancellation.

open_extended.purpose: Open a pathname with extended file-security creation attributes.
open_extended.mechanism: Copies the filesec using `kauth_copyinfilesec`, builds vnode attributes, calls `open1`, then releases copied security storage on return.

open_dprotected_np.purpose: Open with explicit data-protection class/flags, optionally relative to a directory descriptor.
open_dprotected_np.mechanism: `openat_dprotected_internal` carries protection attributes into the common open machinery; actual content-protection behavior remains filesystem-dependent.

openat_dprotected_np.purpose: Open with explicit data-protection class/flags, optionally relative to a directory descriptor.
openat_dprotected_np.mechanism: `openat_dprotected_internal` carries protection attributes into the common open machinery; actual content-protection behavior remains filesystem-dependent.

openbyid_np.purpose: Open a filesystem object selected by filesystem/object identity.
openbyid_np.mechanism: Checks permission to open by ID, resolves a path through `fsgetpath_internal`, then uses `openat_internal`; identity resolution does not bypass the ordinary open operation.

sys_close.purpose: Close a descriptor and release its open-file ownership.
sys_close.mechanism: Both call `close_nocancel` with the current credential; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation. Descriptor removal, drain and final file-operation close are distinct stages underneath.

sys_close_nocancel.purpose: Close a descriptor and release its open-file ownership.
sys_close_nocancel.mechanism: Both call `close_nocancel` with the current credential; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation. Descriptor removal, drain and final file-operation close are distinct stages underneath.

sys_dup.purpose: Allocate another descriptor referring to the same open-file description.
sys_dup.mechanism: Under fd-table protection, checks guard restrictions, reserves a slot with `fdalloc`, and calls `finishdup` to retain the fileglob and publish a new fileproc.

sys_dup2.purpose: Replace a specified descriptor with a duplicate of another.
sys_dup2.mechanism: `dup2` handles source/target identity, reservations, guarded close and target replacement; it can restart while a target slot is reserved before `finishdup` publishes the duplicate.

sys_getdtablesize.purpose: Return the process's current descriptor limit.
sys_getdtablesize.mechanism: Reads the effective nofile limit through `proc_limitgetcur_nofile`; it is a limit query, not a count of open descriptors.

sys_fcntl.mechanism: The common switch handles descriptor flags/duplication, file flags, offsets, advisory locks, leases, preallocation, signatures and other command families, dispatching to file/VNOP or UBC helpers as appropriate. The ordinary entry tests cancellation; this catalog does not enumerate every command ABI.

sys_fcntl_nocancel.mechanism: The common switch handles descriptor flags/duplication, file flags, offsets, advisory locks, leases, preallocation, signatures and other command families, dispatching to file/VNOP or UBC helpers as appropriate. The ordinary entry tests cancellation; this catalog does not enumerate every command ABI.

ioctl.purpose: Issue a control request to the object represented by a descriptor.
ioctl.mechanism: Decodes IOC direction/size, imports a bounded command buffer, looks up the fileproc and applies MAC checks, handles generic descriptor controls, then uses file-operation ioctl dispatch; device-specific command semantics live behind that callback.

sys_flock.purpose: Acquire or release whole-file advisory locking on an open file.
sys_flock.mechanism: Obtains the vnode/fileproc, translates operation flags and invokes `VNOP_ADVLOCK` with flock ownership; retains the references across the lock operation and drops them afterward.

sys_fileport_makeport.purpose: Export a sendable open-file description as a Mach fileport.
sys_fileport_makeport.mechanism: Checks guard/sendability, retains the fileglob, allocates a fileport and copies a send right into the task's IPC space; copyout failures unwind the acquired ownership.

sys_fileport_makefd.purpose: Create a descriptor from a Mach fileport.
sys_fileport_makefd.mechanism: Copies in a typed fileport send right, calls `fileport_makefd` to reserve/publish descriptor state, then releases the temporary port right.

guarded_open_np.purpose: Create an open descriptor with caller-specified guard identity/restrictions, optionally data protection.
guarded_open_np.mechanism: Copies the guard value, builds vnode/open attributes and calls `open1` with guard state; later operations must satisfy the guard contract, not merely possess the numeric fd.

guarded_open_dprotected_np.purpose: Create an open descriptor with caller-specified guard identity/restrictions, optionally data protection.
guarded_open_dprotected_np.mechanism: Copies the guard value, builds vnode/open attributes and calls `open1` with guard state; later operations must satisfy the guard contract, not merely possess the numeric fd.

guarded_close_np.purpose: Close a descriptor only under the matching guard contract.
guarded_close_np.mechanism: Copies the guard, uses `fp_lookup_guarded` under fd protection, then calls `fp_close_and_unlock`; guard mismatch is distinct from ordinary lookup failure.

change_fdguard_np.purpose: Install, replace or remove a descriptor's guard identity and flags.
change_fdguard_np.mechanism: Copies guard inputs, prepares a guarded fileproc, validates/replaces protected fd state under the descriptor lock, and reports the old/new state through the requested output.

guarded_write_np.purpose: Write through a descriptor while supplying its guard identity.
guarded_write_np.mechanism: Copies the guard and calls `write_internal` with it, sharing ordinary transfer machinery while preserving guard checks.

guarded_pwrite_np.purpose: Perform a positional write with a descriptor guard identity.
guarded_pwrite_np.mechanism: Copies the guard and passes it with offset/positional flags to `write_internal`.

guarded_writev_np.purpose: Perform a gather-write with a descriptor guard identity.
guarded_writev_np.mechanism: Copies the guard and invokes `writev_uio`; iovec import and file-operation dispatch remain the common vector-I/O path.

lseek.purpose: Query or change an open file's shared offset, including supported data/hole queries.
lseek.mechanism: Gets the fileglob/vnode, rejects unsuitable objects, applies offset authorization and computes the requested origin; filesystem ioctl handling supports selected seek modes before publishing the offset.

pipe.purpose: Allocate a connected anonymous pipe pair and return both descriptors.
pipe.mechanism: Allocates pipepair storage and two fileprocs, associates endpoint data and labels, then releases reserved fd slots into the table; failed construction closes/frees the partially built endpoints.

link.purpose: Create a hard link, with the *at form accepting directory descriptors and lookup flags.
link.mechanism: `linkat_internal` resolves source/destination, checks authorization and same-filesystem constraints, then performs the vnode link operation and releases lookup references.

linkat.purpose: Create a hard link, with the *at form accepting directory descriptors and lookup flags.
linkat.mechanism: `linkat_internal` resolves source/destination, checks authorization and same-filesystem constraints, then performs the vnode link operation and releases lookup references.

unlink.purpose: Remove a pathname through the shared unlink implementation.
unlink.mechanism: `unlinkat_internal` selects the operation's compatibility flags, resolves parent/target state and performs authorized vnode removal; name removal is distinct from final vnode/open-file destruction.

delete.purpose: Remove a pathname through the shared unlink implementation.
delete.mechanism: `unlinkat_internal` selects the operation's compatibility flags, resolves parent/target state and performs authorized vnode removal; name removal is distinct from final vnode/open-file destruction.

unlinkat.purpose: Remove a directory-relative name or, with the directory flag, a directory.
unlinkat.mechanism: Selects `rmdirat_internal` for directory removal or `unlinkat_internal` otherwise, retaining the caller's directory-fd/flag semantics.

rename.purpose: Rename filesystem names; *at variants supply directory descriptors and the extended variant supplies operation flags.
rename.mechanism: `renameat_internal` coordinates both lookups, compound-operation/retry paths, authorization and the filesystem rename operation. Extended swap/exclusive semantics are flag-selected branches, not separate syscalls.

renameat.purpose: Rename filesystem names; *at variants supply directory descriptors and the extended variant supplies operation flags.
renameat.mechanism: `renameat_internal` coordinates both lookups, compound-operation/retry paths, authorization and the filesystem rename operation. Extended swap/exclusive semantics are flag-selected branches, not separate syscalls.

renameatx_np.purpose: Rename filesystem names; *at variants supply directory descriptors and the extended variant supplies operation flags.
renameatx_np.mechanism: `renameat_internal` coordinates both lookups, compound-operation/retry paths, authorization and the filesystem rename operation. Extended swap/exclusive semantics are flag-selected branches, not separate syscalls.

symlink.purpose: Create a symbolic link containing the supplied target string.
symlink.mechanism: `symlinkat_internal` imports the link content and resolves/creates the destination under the selected directory context, then dispatches the vnode creation operation.

symlinkat.purpose: Create a symbolic link containing the supplied target string.
symlinkat.mechanism: `symlinkat_internal` imports the link content and resolves/creates the destination under the selected directory context, then dispatches the vnode creation operation.

readlink.purpose: Read a symlink's stored target bytes without following its final component.
readlink.mechanism: `readlinkat_internal` uses the requested lookup base and a user buffer/uio, then calls the vnode readlink operation; returned bytes need not include a terminating NUL.

readlinkat.purpose: Read a symlink's stored target bytes without following its final component.
readlinkat.mechanism: `readlinkat_internal` uses the requested lookup base and a user buffer/uio, then calls the vnode readlink operation; returned bytes need not include a terminating NUL.

freadlink.purpose: Read symlink content through an existing descriptor.
freadlink.mechanism: Takes a vnode reference from the descriptor, passes that vnode to `readlinkat_internal`, and drops it after the read.

sys_chdir.purpose: Set the current-directory context for the process or current pthread, respectively.
sys_chdir.mechanism: `common_chdir` resolves/checks a directory and selects process-wide or per-thread state according to the entry's mode; it replaces references rather than just storing the user pathname.

__pthread_chdir.purpose: Set the current-directory context for the process or current pthread, respectively.
__pthread_chdir.mechanism: `common_chdir` resolves/checks a directory and selects process-wide or per-thread state according to the entry's mode; it replaces references rather than just storing the user pathname.

sys_fchdir.purpose: Set process or per-thread current-directory context from an open descriptor.
sys_fchdir.mechanism: The shared `fchdir` helper obtains and checks the descriptor's directory vnode and updates the selected directory context with reference ownership.

__pthread_fchdir.purpose: Set process or per-thread current-directory context from an open descriptor.
__pthread_fchdir.mechanism: The shared `fchdir` helper obtains and checks the descriptor's directory vnode and updates the selected directory context with reference ownership.

chroot.purpose: Change the process's root-directory lookup context.
chroot.mechanism: Requires the local privilege/entitlement checks, resolves the directory through `change_dir`, applies MAC policy and replaces root/cwd-related vnode state; it is not a separate filesystem namespace implementation.

mknod.purpose: Create a filesystem node, including eligible special-device nodes.
mknod.mechanism: Builds vnode attributes from mode/device inputs and calls `mknodat_internal` using current-directory or directory-fd lookup semantics.

mknodat.purpose: Create a filesystem node, including eligible special-device nodes.
mknodat.mechanism: Builds vnode attributes from mode/device inputs and calls `mknodat_internal` using current-directory or directory-fd lookup semantics.

mkfifo.purpose: Create a named pipe node, with optional directory-fd or extended security attributes.
mkfifo.mechanism: Builds vnode creation attributes and uses `mkfifo1`; the extended form first imports/frees filesec storage. Opening the resulting FIFO later constructs its data-transfer state.

mkfifoat.purpose: Create a named pipe node, with optional directory-fd or extended security attributes.
mkfifoat.mechanism: Builds vnode creation attributes and uses `mkfifo1`; the extended form first imports/frees filesec storage. Opening the resulting FIFO later constructs its data-transfer state.

mkfifo_extended.purpose: Create a named pipe node, with optional directory-fd or extended security attributes.
mkfifo_extended.mechanism: Builds vnode creation attributes and uses `mkfifo1`; the extended form first imports/frees filesec storage. Opening the resulting FIFO later constructs its data-transfer state.

mkdir.purpose: Create a directory, with optional directory-relative lookup or extended security attributes.
mkdir.mechanism: Builds creation attributes and calls `mkdir1at`; the extended form imports/frees filesec data. Namespace publication occurs in the filesystem operation, not at argument copyin.

mkdirat.purpose: Create a directory, with optional directory-relative lookup or extended security attributes.
mkdirat.mechanism: Builds creation attributes and calls `mkdir1at`; the extended form imports/frees filesec data. Namespace publication occurs in the filesystem operation, not at argument copyin.

mkdir_extended.purpose: Create a directory, with optional directory-relative lookup or extended security attributes.
mkdir_extended.mechanism: Builds creation attributes and calls `mkdir1at`; the extended form imports/frees filesec data. Namespace publication occurs in the filesystem operation, not at argument copyin.

rmdir.purpose: Remove an empty directory by pathname.
rmdir.mechanism: `rmdirat_internal` coordinates directory lookup/authorization and vnode removal, including the normal lookup cleanup.

revoke.purpose: Invalidate access through eligible character/block-device vnodes and aliases.
revoke.mechanism: Resolves the vnode, checks type/mount/ownership/MAC restrictions, and invokes `VNOP_REVOKE`; it does not implement generic regular-file descriptor revocation.

undelete.purpose: Retain a historical undelete syscall number without an implementation.
undelete.mechanism: The local handler immediately returns `ENOTSUP`; no name restoration or filesystem operation occurs.

clonefileat.purpose: Clone a source pathname into a destination directory/name.
clonefileat.mechanism: Resolves source identity, then `clonefile_internal` validates and dispatches cloning to the filesystem. Copy-on-write extent behavior depends on that filesystem implementation.

fclonefileat.purpose: Clone an open source file into a destination directory/name.
fclonefileat.mechanism: Pins the source fileproc/vnode, calls `clonefile_internal`, and drops both references on completion; filesystem cloning remains behind the VNOP boundary.

copyfile.purpose: Request the filesystem-level copyfile operation between names.
copyfile.mechanism: Resolves source/destination, checks MAC/authorization and leases, and invokes `VNOP_COPYFILE`; this syscall is not the entire userspace copyfile library's fallback implementation.

exchangedata.purpose: Exchange data between eligible regular files.
exchangedata.mechanism: Resolves both vnodes, authorizes the exchange, handles lease/event bookkeeping and dispatches the filesystem exchange operation; its storage implementation is external for absent filesystems.

stat.purpose: Read status for a pathname while following its final symlink, using the declared legacy/64-bit and optional filesec ABI.
stat.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` resolves the vnode and marshals status/security output according to flags supplied by each wrapper; size/ABI variants share lookup and attribute collection rather than a different filesystem operation.

stat64.purpose: Read status for a pathname while following its final symlink, using the declared legacy/64-bit and optional filesec ABI.
stat64.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` resolves the vnode and marshals status/security output according to flags supplied by each wrapper; size/ABI variants share lookup and attribute collection rather than a different filesystem operation.

stat_extended.purpose: Read status for a pathname while following its final symlink, using the declared legacy/64-bit and optional filesec ABI.
stat_extended.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` resolves the vnode and marshals status/security output according to flags supplied by each wrapper; size/ABI variants share lookup and attribute collection rather than a different filesystem operation.

stat64_extended.purpose: Read status for a pathname while following its final symlink, using the declared legacy/64-bit and optional filesec ABI.
stat64_extended.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` resolves the vnode and marshals status/security output according to flags supplied by each wrapper; size/ABI variants share lookup and attribute collection rather than a different filesystem operation.

lstat.purpose: Read status for the final pathname component itself, including a symlink, using the declared ABI.
lstat.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` receives no-follow semantics and the wrapper's legacy/64-bit/filesec options, then collects and copies out vnode attributes.

lstat64.purpose: Read status for the final pathname component itself, including a symlink, using the declared ABI.
lstat64.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` receives no-follow semantics and the wrapper's legacy/64-bit/filesec options, then collects and copies out vnode attributes.

lstat_extended.purpose: Read status for the final pathname component itself, including a symlink, using the declared ABI.
lstat_extended.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` receives no-follow semantics and the wrapper's legacy/64-bit/filesec options, then collects and copies out vnode attributes.

lstat64_extended.purpose: Read status for the final pathname component itself, including a symlink, using the declared ABI.
lstat64_extended.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` receives no-follow semantics and the wrapper's legacy/64-bit/filesec options, then collects and copies out vnode attributes.

fstatat.purpose: Read status relative to a directory descriptor with explicit lookup flags.
fstatat.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` carries the directory base, follow/no-follow flags and status ABI into common pathname and attribute handling.

fstatat64.purpose: Read status relative to a directory descriptor with explicit lookup flags.
fstatat64.mechanism: `fstatat_internal` carries the directory base, follow/no-follow flags and status ABI into common pathname and attribute handling.

sys_fstat.purpose: Read status from an open descriptor using its declared status/filesec ABI.
sys_fstat.mechanism: The shared `fstat` helper references the fileproc and invokes the file type's stat operation; wrappers select layout and extended-security arguments.

sys_fstat64.purpose: Read status from an open descriptor using its declared status/filesec ABI.
sys_fstat64.mechanism: The shared `fstat` helper references the fileproc and invokes the file type's stat operation; wrappers select layout and extended-security arguments.

sys_fstat_extended.purpose: Read status from an open descriptor using its declared status/filesec ABI.
sys_fstat_extended.mechanism: The shared `fstat` helper references the fileproc and invokes the file type's stat operation; wrappers select layout and extended-security arguments.

sys_fstat64_extended.purpose: Read status from an open descriptor using its declared status/filesec ABI.
sys_fstat64_extended.mechanism: The shared `fstat` helper references the fileproc and invokes the file type's stat operation; wrappers select layout and extended-security arguments.

pathconf.mechanism: Resolves a vnode and invokes `vn_pathconf`, then releases pathname and vnode references; the requested name selects the queried limit.

sys_fpathconf.purpose: Query an implementation limit through a descriptor.
sys_fpathconf.mechanism: Looks up the fileproc, obtains its vnode where applicable, and calls `vn_pathconf` with the selected name before dropping references.

chmod.purpose: Change permission mode for a pathname, optionally relative to a directory fd.
chmod.mechanism: `fchmodat_internal` applies lookup flags and invokes the shared authorization/setattr path; directory-relative selection is not an alternate credential model.

fchmodat.purpose: Change permission mode for a pathname, optionally relative to a directory fd.
fchmodat.mechanism: `fchmodat_internal` applies lookup flags and invokes the shared authorization/setattr path; directory-relative selection is not an alternate credential model.

fchmod.purpose: Change permission mode through an open descriptor.
fchmod.mechanism: Builds a vnode-attribute request and passes it to `fchmod1`, which resolves the descriptor vnode and performs the authorized change.

chmod_extended.purpose: Change permissions and extended file-security attributes by path or descriptor.
chmod_extended.mechanism: `chmod_extended_init` imports filesec state, then `chmodat` or `fchmod1` performs the change; copied security storage is freed on completion.

fchmod_extended.purpose: Change permissions and extended file-security attributes by path or descriptor.
fchmod_extended.mechanism: `chmod_extended_init` imports filesec state, then `chmodat` or `fchmod1` performs the change; copied security storage is freed on completion.

chown.purpose: Change owner/group of a pathname, optionally relative to a directory fd.
chown.mechanism: `fchownat_internal` resolves with the wrapper's follow and directory-base rules, then applies vnode ownership authorization and attributes.

fchownat.purpose: Change owner/group of a pathname, optionally relative to a directory fd.
fchownat.mechanism: `fchownat_internal` resolves with the wrapper's follow and directory-base rules, then applies vnode ownership authorization and attributes.

lchown.purpose: Change ownership of the final pathname component without following a symlink.
lchown.mechanism: Uses `fchownat_internal` with no-follow semantics rather than changing the referenced symlink target.

fchown.purpose: Change ownership of an open file.
fchown.mechanism: Pins the descriptor vnode, calls `vn_chown_internal`, then releases the vnode and descriptor references.

chflags.purpose: Change filesystem flags by pathname or descriptor.
chflags.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, handle applicable lease breaking, and call `chflags1`; allowed flags and ownership checks are enforced in the common attribute path.

fchflags.purpose: Change filesystem flags by pathname or descriptor.
fchflags.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, handle applicable lease breaking, and call `chflags1`; allowed flags and ownership checks are enforced in the common attribute path.

access.purpose: Test requested pathname access using access-check credential semantics, optionally relative to a directory fd.
access.mechanism: `faccessat_internal` performs the requested lookup/flag handling and permission test; it is not a reservation guaranteeing that a later open will still succeed.

faccessat.purpose: Test requested pathname access using access-check credential semantics, optionally relative to a directory fd.
faccessat.mechanism: `faccessat_internal` performs the requested lookup/flag handling and permission test; it is not a reservation guaranteeing that a later open will still succeed.

access_extended.purpose: Perform a batch of extended pathname access tests.
access_extended.mechanism: Imports the descriptor/path test buffer, derives real-identity credentials, resolves each selected name and uses `access1`, reporting per-test results under the packed interface contract.

umask.purpose: Replace the process creation mask and, for the extended form, associated security mask state.
umask.mechanism: Both enter `umask1`, which updates the creation policy used by later vnode creation; existing file permissions are not changed.

umask_extended.purpose: Replace the process creation mask and, for the extended form, associated security mask state.
umask_extended.mechanism: Both enter `umask1`, which updates the creation policy used by later vnode creation; existing file permissions are not changed.

utimes.purpose: Set file timestamps by pathname or descriptor.
utimes.mechanism: `getutimes` imports/converts the supplied time values, then `setutimes` performs the vnode update after lookup and lease handling.

futimes.purpose: Set file timestamps by pathname or descriptor.
futimes.mechanism: `getutimes` imports/converts the supplied time values, then `setutimes` performs the vnode update after lookup and lease handling.

truncate.mechanism: Validates the requested length, resolves the vnode and invokes `truncate_internal`; shrinking/growing cache and filesystem state is delegated to the vnode/UBC path.

ftruncate.purpose: Change the length of an open file or POSIX shared-memory object.
ftruncate.mechanism: Dispatches POSIX shared memory to `pshm_truncate`; eligible vnode descriptors pass validation and `truncate_internal`, with fileproc/vnode references held across the operation.

getattrlist.purpose: Read a requested bitmap of filesystem attributes into a packed user buffer.
getattrlist.mechanism: Imports `attrlist`, resolves through `getattrlistat_internal`, and assembles the selected attributes using the user ABI, options and directory base.

getattrlistat.purpose: Read a requested bitmap of filesystem attributes into a packed user buffer.
getattrlistat.mechanism: Imports `attrlist`, resolves through `getattrlistat_internal`, and assembles the selected attributes using the user ABI, options and directory base.

fgetattrlist.purpose: Read packed filesystem attributes from an open vnode descriptor.
fgetattrlist.mechanism: Obtains a typed fileproc and vnode reference, imports the requested bitmap and invokes `getattrlist_internal`, then releases both references.

setattrlist.purpose: Set a bitmap-selected packed set of filesystem attributes by path, directory-relative path or descriptor.
setattrlist.mechanism: Each entry resolves/pins its vnode, handles lease interaction and calls `setattrlist_internal`, which validates bitmap/layout and performs the attribute update.

setattrlistat.purpose: Set a bitmap-selected packed set of filesystem attributes by path, directory-relative path or descriptor.
setattrlistat.mechanism: Each entry resolves/pins its vnode, handles lease interaction and calls `setattrlist_internal`, which validates bitmap/layout and performs the attribute update.

fsetattrlist.purpose: Set a bitmap-selected packed set of filesystem attributes by path, directory-relative path or descriptor.
fsetattrlist.mechanism: Each entry resolves/pins its vnode, handles lease interaction and calls `setattrlist_internal`, which validates bitmap/layout and performs the attribute update.

getattrlistbulk.purpose: Read packed attributes for multiple directory entries while advancing directory enumeration state.
getattrlistbulk.mechanism: Pins a directory fileproc/vnode, imports the attribute selection and uses the bulk directory-attribute path; output capacity and returned entry count bound progress.

getdirentries.purpose: Read directory records and return the enumeration base offset using the declared record ABI.
getdirentries.mechanism: `getdirentries_common` drives directory reading and shared offset handling; wrappers choose legacy/64-bit layout and copy the resulting base offset out separately.

getdirentries64.purpose: Read directory records and return the enumeration base offset using the declared record ABI.
getdirentries64.mechanism: `getdirentries_common` drives directory reading and shared offset handling; wrappers choose legacy/64-bit layout and copy the resulting base offset out separately.

getdirentriesattr.purpose: Enumerate directory entries with requested attributes through the older packed interface.
getdirentriesattr.mechanism: Imports attrlist/count inputs, holds the directory fileglob offset lock, drives the directory-attribute vnode operation and copies updated enumeration/output counts back.

getxattr.purpose: Read an extended attribute by path or descriptor, or query its size.
getxattr.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, copy and validate the attribute name including protected-name rules, and call `vn_getxattr` with a user `uio` when a data buffer is supplied.

fgetxattr.purpose: Read an extended attribute by path or descriptor, or query its size.
fgetxattr.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, copy and validate the attribute name including protected-name rules, and call `vn_getxattr` with a user `uio` when a data buffer is supplied.

setxattr.purpose: Create or replace an extended attribute by path or descriptor.
setxattr.mechanism: Validate name/options/protected-attribute permissions, build a user `uio`, handle applicable leases and call `vn_setxattr`; successful changes can generate filesystem events.

fsetxattr.purpose: Create or replace an extended attribute by path or descriptor.
fsetxattr.mechanism: Validate name/options/protected-attribute permissions, build a user `uio`, handle applicable leases and call `vn_setxattr`; successful changes can generate filesystem events.

removexattr.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, validate the name/options and call `vn_removexattr`, with lease and filesystem-event handling around a successful mutation.

fremovexattr.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, validate the name/options and call `vn_removexattr`, with lease and filesystem-event handling around a successful mutation.

listxattr.purpose: List a file's extended-attribute names or query required size.
listxattr.mechanism: Build the appropriate user `uio` after path/fd lookup and call `vn_listxattr`; residual/output sizing controls the returned byte count.

flistxattr.purpose: List a file's extended-attribute names or query required size.
flistxattr.mechanism: Build the appropriate user `uio` after path/fd lookup and call `vn_listxattr`; residual/output sizing controls the returned byte count.

searchfs.purpose: Search a filesystem using packed attribute predicates and continuation state.
searchfs.mechanism: Under `CONFIG_SEARCHFS`, the handler imports search parameters, resolves the filesystem root and invokes `VNOP_SEARCHFS` with a user `uio`; without it the alternate body returns `ENOTSUP`. Matching indexes inside absent filesystems are not implemented here.

fsgetpath.purpose: Resolve filesystem/object identity to a pathname, with extended options where declared.
fsgetpath.mechanism: `fsgetpath_extended` performs identity lookup and path construction through `fsgetpath_internal`, then copies the result to the supplied buffer subject to access and size checks.

fsgetpath_ext.purpose: Resolve filesystem/object identity to a pathname, with extended options where declared.
fsgetpath_ext.mechanism: `fsgetpath_extended` performs identity lookup and path construction through `fsgetpath_internal`, then copies the result to the supplied buffer subject to access and size checks.

mount.purpose: Mount or update a filesystem, with optional MAC-label input in the extended entry.
mount.mechanism: `mount` forwards to `__mac_mount`; the latter imports type/options, resolves the mount point and enters `mount_common`/filesystem mount dispatch, coordinating authorization and publication.

__mac_mount.purpose: Mount or update a filesystem, with optional MAC-label input in the extended entry.
__mac_mount.mechanism: `mount` forwards to `__mac_mount`; the latter imports type/options, resolves the mount point and enters `mount_common`/filesystem mount dispatch, coordinating authorization and publication.

fmount.purpose: Mount using an already-open mount-point descriptor.
fmount.mechanism: Imports the filesystem type, obtains the vnode and parent/path context, then calls `mount_common`; supported update cases can use the shared MAC mount path.

unmount.purpose: Unmount a filesystem selected by path or descriptor.
unmount.mechanism: Resolve and retain the mount, apply mount/MAC checks and call `safedounmount`; busy/drain and failed-unmount state belong to the common VFS teardown path.

funmount.purpose: Unmount a filesystem selected by path or descriptor.
funmount.mechanism: Resolve and retain the mount, apply mount/MAC checks and call `safedounmount`; busy/drain and failed-unmount state belong to the common VFS teardown path.

statfs.purpose: Read filesystem statistics by path or open descriptor using the legacy ABI.
statfs.mechanism: Resolve a vnode and call `statfs_internal`, which updates/collects mount information and copies the selected filesystem-stat structure.

fstatfs.purpose: Read filesystem statistics by path or open descriptor using the legacy ABI.
fstatfs.mechanism: Resolve a vnode and call `statfs_internal`, which updates/collects mount information and copies the selected filesystem-stat structure.

statfs64.purpose: Read filesystem statistics using the 64-bit statfs layout.
statfs64.mechanism: Pin the vnode/mount, apply mount-stat authorization, call `vfs_update_vfsstat`/`vfs_get_statfs64`, and copy the assembled record out.

fstatfs64.purpose: Read filesystem statistics using the 64-bit statfs layout.
fstatfs64.mechanism: Pin the vnode/mount, apply mount-stat authorization, call `vfs_update_vfsstat`/`vfs_get_statfs64`, and copy the assembled record out.

getfsstat.purpose: Enumerate mounted filesystem statistics, optionally with MAC label output.
getfsstat.mechanism: Use `vfs_iterate` and size-limited output callbacks; the legacy entry delegates to `__mac_getfsstat`, while the 64-bit entry selects its own record layout.

getfsstat64.purpose: Enumerate mounted filesystem statistics, optionally with MAC label output.
getfsstat64.mechanism: Use `vfs_iterate` and size-limited output callbacks; the legacy entry delegates to `__mac_getfsstat`, while the 64-bit entry selects its own record layout.

__mac_getfsstat.purpose: Enumerate mounted filesystem statistics, optionally with MAC label output.
__mac_getfsstat.mechanism: Use `vfs_iterate` and size-limited output callbacks; the legacy entry delegates to `__mac_getfsstat`, while the 64-bit entry selects its own record layout.

__mac_get_mount.purpose: Read a mount's externalized MAC label by pathname.
__mac_get_mount.mechanism: Resolve/retain the mount, invoke `mac_mount_label_get`, and drop the mount reference after output handling.

sync.purpose: Request synchronization of mounted filesystems and report dirty-buffer accounting internally.
sync.mechanism: `vfs_iterate` visits eligible mounts for sync work; VM/buffer statistics are consulted separately. It is not a per-fd completion token or a universal hardware durability guarantee.

fsync.purpose: Synchronize an open file; fdatasync selects the data-focused common mode.
fsync.mechanism: All reach `fsync_common`, which performs file/vnode synchronization. Ordinary fsync and fdatasync test cancellation; fsync_nocancel directly enters the common operation.

fsync_nocancel.purpose: Synchronize an open file; fdatasync selects the data-focused common mode.
fsync_nocancel.mechanism: All reach `fsync_common`, which performs file/vnode synchronization. Ordinary fsync and fdatasync test cancellation; fsync_nocancel directly enters the common operation.

fdatasync.purpose: Synchronize an open file; fdatasync selects the data-focused common mode.
fdatasync.mechanism: All reach `fsync_common`, which performs file/vnode synchronization. Ordinary fsync and fdatasync test cancellation; fsync_nocancel directly enters the common operation.

fsctl.purpose: Issue filesystem-specific control commands by path or descriptor.
fsctl.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, apply mount-control MAC checks and call `fsctl_internal`. It rejects character/block vnodes with `ENOTTY`, decodes common commands and forwards permitted filesystem-specific controls through `VNOP_IOCTL`. Output copyout occurs after the operation and can fail independently. This catalog scopes the multiplexor, not every filesystem-private command. See [type rejection](../../../xnu/bsd/vfs/vfs_syscalls.c#L13398) and [filesystem dispatch/output](../../../xnu/bsd/vfs/vfs_syscalls.c#L13679).

ffsctl.purpose: Issue filesystem-specific control commands by path or descriptor.
ffsctl.mechanism: Resolve/pin the vnode, apply mount-control MAC checks and call `fsctl_internal`. It rejects character/block vnodes with `ENOTTY`, decodes common commands and forwards permitted filesystem-specific controls through `VNOP_IOCTL`. Output copyout occurs after the operation and can fail independently. This catalog scopes the multiplexor, not every filesystem-private command. See [type rejection](../../../xnu/bsd/vfs/vfs_syscalls.c#L13398) and [filesystem dispatch/output](../../../xnu/bsd/vfs/vfs_syscalls.c#L13679).

quotactl.purpose: Manage or query filesystem quota state.
quotactl.mechanism: Under `QUOTA`, the handler imports command-specific data and invokes `VFS_QUOTACTL` while holding a mount reference; without it the alternate body returns `EOPNOTSUPP`. Commands include quota-file/control and per-ID usage/limit operations.

fs_snapshot.purpose: Manage filesystem snapshots through a directory fd and operation selector.
fs_snapshot.mechanism: Checks snapshot authorization, resolves mount/root objects and dispatches create/delete/rename/mount/revert-related helpers. Actual snapshot storage is a filesystem operation, not reconstructed APFS code.

pivot_root.purpose: Switch the root filesystem under the supported platform/authorization configuration.
pivot_root.mechanism: Under `XNU_TARGET_OS_OSX`, the handler validates privileged inputs and calls `vfs_switch_root` after vnode/ioctl checks; the alternate definition invokes `nosys`. It is not enabled uniformly merely because a master number exists.

graftdmg.purpose: Graft an authenticated disk-image/cryptex filesystem at a mount location.
graftdmg.mechanism: Imports the type-specific argument union, pins source/target vnodes, checks entitlements/MAC and calls the secure-boot graft helper, then sends policy notifications and releases lookup state.

ungraftdmg.mechanism: Checks entitlement/MAC policy, resolves the target, issues the filesystem ungraft ioctl and performs notification/reference cleanup.

vfs_purge.purpose: Request privileged purge of filesystem caches/file-backed pager resources.
vfs_purge.mechanism: Iterates VFS purge callbacks and calls `vm_purge_filebacked_pagers`; it is broader than closing descriptors and does not imply every referenced vnode can be destroyed.

nfssvc.purpose: Operate the in-kernel NFS server using an operation flag set.
nfssvc.mechanism: Privilege/MAC checks precede socket installation, server-worker entry, export management or statistics helpers such as `nfssvc_addsock`, `nfssvc_nfsd` and `nfssvc_export`; peer/server protocol work lives in the NFS implementation.

getfh.purpose: Obtain an exported filesystem handle for a pathname.
getfh.mechanism: Resolves the vnode and export context under NFS export protection, translates to an NFS filehandle and copies the bounded result out; requires appropriate privilege/server support.

fhopen.purpose: Open an exported object using a filehandle.
fhopen.mechanism: Imports the handle, resolves it with `nfsrv_fhtovp` under export protection, then validates vnode/open rights and constructs descriptor state.

mmap.purpose: Create a process virtual mapping from anonymous memory or a supported descriptor.
mmap.mechanism: Sanitizes address/size/protection/flags, resolves file or shared-memory backing and authorization, then enters Mach VM mapping with translated inheritance/copy/protection options; the returned address is copied through the syscall result ABI.

munmap.mechanism: `munmap_sanitize` checks/normalizes the range before `mach_vm_deallocate_kernel` removes it from the current map; error conversion is handled at the BSD boundary.

mprotect.purpose: Change requested protections on a virtual range.
mprotect.mechanism: Sanitizes range/protection, applies MAC/code-signing checks and invokes `mach_vm_protect`; maximum protection and map/pmap policy can reject the change.

msync.purpose: Synchronize mapped memory according to the requested flags.
msync.mechanism: `msync_nocancel` sanitizes the range and calls `mach_vm_msync`; the ordinary wrapper first tests cancellation. This operation is distinct from descriptor fsync.

msync_nocancel.purpose: Synchronize mapped memory according to the requested flags.
msync_nocancel.mechanism: `msync_nocancel` sanitizes the range and calls `mach_vm_msync`; the ordinary wrapper first tests cancellation. This operation is distinct from descriptor fsync.

madvise.purpose: Apply a virtual-memory behavior/advice request to a range.
madvise.mechanism: `madvise_sanitize` validates the behavior/range, then `mach_vm_behavior_set` selects the VM operation; advice modes have different reclaim/read-ahead semantics.

minherit.purpose: Change a mapping's fork inheritance behavior.
minherit.mechanism: Sanitizes the range and inheritance value and calls `mach_vm_inherit`; later task/map copying interprets the resulting entry policy.

mincore.purpose: Report per-page residency/status information for a virtual range.
mincore.mechanism: Sanitizes the range, queries batches with `vm_map_page_range_info_internal`, translates page-state bits and copies the result vector out.

mlock.purpose: Wire a user virtual-address range into memory.
mlock.mechanism: Calls `vm_map_wire_kernel` for the current map with user-wiring semantics and translated protection; accounting, faults and resource-limit failures remain VM responsibilities.

munlock.purpose: Remove user wiring from a range.
munlock.mechanism: Calls `vm_map_unwire` for the current map/range; releasing a wiring claim is not necessarily freeing the physical page.

mlockall.purpose: Preserve declared whole-address-space wiring entry points without a local implementation.
mlockall.mechanism: Each handler immediately returns `ENOSYS`; these numbers do not provide functioning whole-map lock/unlock operations in this checkout.

munlockall.purpose: Preserve declared whole-address-space wiring entry points without a local implementation.
munlockall.mechanism: Each handler immediately returns `ENOSYS`; these numbers do not provide functioning whole-map lock/unlock operations in this checkout.

swapon.purpose: Preserve a historical swap-enable entry point.
swapon.mechanism: The body returns `ENOTSUP`; actual compressor/swap lifecycle is not configured through this legacy syscall here.

shared_region_check_np.purpose: Query/establish the process's shared-region association and start address.
shared_region_check_np.mechanism: Uses `vm_shared_region_get` and shared-region validation/removal paths, considers task address width and mapping state, then returns the shared-region address through user output.

shared_region_map_and_slide_2_np.purpose: Map a collection of shared-cache files and slide/fixup metadata into the shared region.
shared_region_map_and_slide_2_np.mechanism: Imports bounded file/mapping arrays through `shared_region_copyin`, validates descriptor-backed mappings, and enters the shared-region map/slide machinery; dyld's external cache production is outside this body.

map_with_linking_np.purpose: Map file-backed regions with kernel-assisted linking metadata.
map_with_linking_np.mechanism: Imports region/linking information, resolves vnode-backed descriptors and UBC objects, applies mmap policy and enters the VM map/linking path; the syscall consumes metadata rather than performing arbitrary userspace linking.

mremap_encrypted.purpose: Install encrypted-image mapping/decryption handling for a virtual range.
mremap_encrypted.mechanism: Sanitizes the range, resolves the mapped vnode/offset identity and selects registered decryption/pager handling; cryptographic provider internals are outside this local frontend.

vm_pressure_monitor.purpose: Query or wait for virtual-memory pressure information.
vm_pressure_monitor.mechanism: Calls `mach_vm_pressure_monitor` with the requested wait/duration policy and copies pressure/reclaim information to the supplied output pointers.

kas_info.purpose: Query selected kernel address-space layout information under privilege and configuration gates.
kas_info.mechanism: The selector dispatch checks `CONFIG_KAS_INFO`, credentials/MAC and user-width/size inputs before copying slide or segment information; unsupported selectors/configurations fail rather than exposing arbitrary kernel memory.

memorystatus_control.purpose: Query or change process memory-status, limits, priority and related jetsam/freezer policy.
memorystatus_control.mechanism: Checks credentials/entitlements/MAC and dispatches the command to `memorystatus_cmd_*` helpers; list/snapshot queries, limit updates and process actions have different payload/ownership contracts.

memorystatus_get_level.mechanism: Copies the maintained level value to the supplied user address; it does not initiate pressure collection or freeze a process.

memorystatus_available_memory.purpose: Estimate memory available to the current process under memorystatus policy.
memorystatus_available_memory.mechanism: Returns `memorystatus_available_memory_internal` through the 64-bit syscall result path, incorporating local limits/availability policy rather than raw free-page count alone.

exit.purpose: Terminate the current process with an exit status.
exit.mechanism: Calls `exit1` with an encoded wait status, then follows thread exception-return/block termination paths; descriptor/task teardown and parent wake/reap are distinct later stages.

fork.purpose: Create a child process/task derived from the caller.
fork.mechanism: `fork1` allocates/clones process/thread state, arranges map/task and return-register state, completes transition/signal coordination and releases the child for execution; failures unwind partial construction.

vfork.purpose: Declare a conditional historical vfork entry point.
vfork.mechanism: `CONFIG_VFORK` selects this master declaration, but no local handler definition is present in this checkout. Comments describing legacy vfork-related execution are not an implementation; the disabled alternative is `nosys`.

execve.purpose: Replace the current executable image, optionally with MAC execution-label input.
execve.mechanism: `execve` forwards to `__mac_execve`, which imports arguments/environment, coordinates replacement proc/task state and invokes image activation; failures before and after the transition's commitment point have different cleanup rules.

__mac_execve.purpose: Replace the current executable image, optionally with MAC execution-label input.
__mac_execve.mechanism: `execve` forwards to `__mac_execve`, which imports arguments/environment, coordinates replacement proc/task state and invokes image activation; failures before and after the transition's commitment point have different cleanup rules.

posix_spawn.purpose: Create or replace a process image with spawn attributes and file actions.
posix_spawn.mechanism: Imports packed attributes/actions, builds the child/replacement process state, applies descriptor/identity actions and image activation, then either publishes success or unwinds construction. It is not just fork followed by an uncoordinated userspace exec.

wait4.purpose: Wait for selected child state and optionally return status/resource usage.
wait4.mechanism: The nocancel body scans children under process-list coordination, waits/retries and copies results before eligible reaping. Ordinary wait4 first performs the cancellation test.

wait4_nocancel.purpose: Wait for selected child state and optionally return status/resource usage.
wait4_nocancel.mechanism: The nocancel body scans children under process-list coordination, waits/retries and copies results before eligible reaping. Ordinary wait4 first performs the cancellation test.

waitid.purpose: Wait for selected child events and return structured siginfo.
waitid.mechanism: The shared body filters children/events using idtype/options, coordinates wait ownership and copies siginfo; options can observe state without consuming it. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

waitid_nocancel.purpose: Wait for selected child events and return structured siginfo.
waitid_nocancel.mechanism: The shared body filters children/events using idtype/options, coordinates wait ownership and copies siginfo; options can observe state without consuming it. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

getpid.mechanism: Reads `proc_getpid(p)` into the syscall result slot; no process lookup or new reference is needed for the current process argument.

getppid.purpose: Return the calling process's recorded parent ID.
getppid.mechanism: Reads the proc parent-ID field into the result slot; it does not acquire a capability to the parent task.

getpgrp.purpose: Return the calling process's process-group ID.
getpgrp.mechanism: Reads the process group identifier from the current proc state into the scalar result.

getpgid.purpose: Return a selected process's process-group ID.
getpgid.mechanism: Uses the current process for PID zero or obtains a referenced process with `proc_find`, reads its group identity and releases the lookup reference.

getsid.purpose: Return a selected process's session ID.
getsid.mechanism: Uses `proc_sessionid`, looking up and releasing another process when a noncurrent PID is requested.

setsid.purpose: Create a new session/process group for an eligible caller.
setsid.mechanism: `setsid_internal` validates session/group restrictions and establishes the new group/session relationship; the wrapper returns the process ID on success.

setpgid.mechanism: Validates caller/child/session and exec restrictions, obtains group references and invokes `enterpgrp`; membership updates are coordinated with proc/group lifetime protection.

getuid.purpose: Read the caller's real/effective user/group ID as selected by the entry.
getuid.mechanism: The four wrappers call `kauth_getruid`, `kauth_getuid`, `kauth_getrgid` or `kauth_getgid`, respectively, and return a scalar identity from the active credential.

geteuid.purpose: Read the caller's real/effective user/group ID as selected by the entry.
geteuid.mechanism: The four wrappers call `kauth_getruid`, `kauth_getuid`, `kauth_getrgid` or `kauth_getgid`, respectively, and return a scalar identity from the active credential.

getgid.purpose: Read the caller's real/effective user/group ID as selected by the entry.
getgid.mechanism: The four wrappers call `kauth_getruid`, `kauth_getuid`, `kauth_getrgid` or `kauth_getgid`, respectively, and return a scalar identity from the active credential.

getegid.purpose: Read the caller's real/effective user/group ID as selected by the entry.
getegid.mechanism: The four wrappers call `kauth_getruid`, `kauth_getuid`, `kauth_getrgid` or `kauth_getgid`, respectively, and return a scalar identity from the active credential.

setuid.purpose: Change real/effective/saved user identity according to the selected API.
setuid.mechanism: Use `kauth_cred_proc_update` with privilege/MAC checks and `kauth_cred_model_setresuid`; credential publication and process-count accounting replace immutable credential state rather than editing a shared credential in place.

seteuid.purpose: Change real/effective/saved user identity according to the selected API.
seteuid.mechanism: Use `kauth_cred_proc_update` with privilege/MAC checks and `kauth_cred_model_setresuid`; credential publication and process-count accounting replace immutable credential state rather than editing a shared credential in place.

setreuid.purpose: Change real/effective/saved user identity according to the selected API.
setreuid.mechanism: Use `kauth_cred_proc_update` with privilege/MAC checks and `kauth_cred_model_setresuid`; credential publication and process-count accounting replace immutable credential state rather than editing a shared credential in place.

setgid.purpose: Change real/effective/saved group identity according to the selected API.
setgid.mechanism: Use `kauth_cred_proc_update`, operation-specific permission/MAC checks and `kauth_cred_model_setresgid`; invalid identity transitions fail before publication.

setegid.purpose: Change real/effective/saved group identity according to the selected API.
setegid.mechanism: Use `kauth_cred_proc_update`, operation-specific permission/MAC checks and `kauth_cred_model_setresgid`; invalid identity transitions fail before publication.

setregid.purpose: Change real/effective/saved group identity according to the selected API.
setregid.mechanism: Use `kauth_cred_proc_update`, operation-specific permission/MAC checks and `kauth_cred_model_setresgid`; invalid identity transitions fail before publication.

getgroups.purpose: Read the caller's supplementary group list or its required count.
getgroups.mechanism: Retains the active credential, accesses `posix_cred_get` group state, checks supplied capacity and copies the array out before releasing the credential.

setgroups.purpose: Replace supplementary groups, with initgroups also supplying the membership identity context.
setgroups.mechanism: `setgroups1` imports and validates the group array and publishes updated credential state; the two wrappers select the corresponding identity/group semantics.

initgroups.purpose: Replace supplementary groups, with initgroups also supplying the membership identity context.
initgroups.mechanism: `setgroups1` imports and validates the group array and publishes updated credential state; the two wrappers select the corresponding identity/group semantics.

getlogin.mechanism: Obtains the process group/session, copies the name under the session lock into kernel storage, releases the group and copies the bounded string to userspace.

setlogin.purpose: Change the session login name under privilege checks.
setlogin.mechanism: Checks `proc_suser`, imports the bounded name and calls `setlogin_internal`; the affected object is session state, not the username fields of every credential.

sys_settid.purpose: Set a thread-specific effective identity override.
sys_settid.mechanism: Passes the requested UID/GID to `kern_settid`, which manages the thread credential override; it is distinct from changing the process credential.

sys_settid_with_pid.purpose: Set thread identity using another process's credential context.
sys_settid_with_pid.mechanism: Obtains a referenced credential by PID, extracts the relevant identity, calls `kern_settid` and releases the temporary credential; PID lookup/policy can fail.

gettid.purpose: Read thread-credential identity into UID/GID outputs.
gettid.mechanism: Examines `current_thread_ro` and copies real UID/GID from the applicable credential context; this historical syscall is not the numeric thread-ID query provided by thread_selfid.

setsgroups.purpose: Retain historical supplementary-group entry points without implementation.
setsgroups.mechanism: These local handlers immediately return `ENOTSUP`; they do not read or change group arrays.

getsgroups.purpose: Retain historical supplementary-group entry points without implementation.
getsgroups.mechanism: These local handlers immediately return `ENOTSUP`; they do not read or change group arrays.

setwgroups.purpose: Retain historical supplementary-group entry points without implementation.
setwgroups.mechanism: These local handlers immediately return `ENOTSUP`; they do not read or change group arrays.

getwgroups.purpose: Retain historical supplementary-group entry points without implementation.
getwgroups.mechanism: These local handlers immediately return `ENOTSUP`; they do not read or change group arrays.

issetugid.purpose: Report whether process execution has acquired the set-ID/security-tainted state.
issetugid.mechanism: Returns `proc_issetugid(p)`; it reports maintained process history/state rather than comparing only current UID and EUID.

setprivexec.purpose: Set the proc's legacy privileged-debugger execution flag and return its previous value.
setprivexec.mechanism: Audits the input, returns `p_debugger`, then stores whether the supplied flag is nonzero. The body is a direct proc-field operation, not a general privilege grant engine.

identitysvc.purpose: Serve kernel identity/group resolver work through a privileged userspace service.
identitysvc.mechanism: Checks entitlement/authorization and dispatches resolver registration, work delivery, completion and cache-related operations under the resolver lock; the directory-service implementation itself is external.

persona.purpose: Create, remove, query or find persona identities through an operation selector.
persona.mechanism: Dispatches to `kpersona_*_syscall` helpers that validate/import identity data and manage persona object/reference lifetime. `CONFIG_PERSONAS` controls whether this declaration is selected.

ptrace.mechanism: Dispatches request-specific attach/detach, signal and state operations after process/credential/platform checks; some requests terminate or alter execution state. It is not a generic unchecked task-memory accessor.

setpriority.purpose: Change or query selected process/group/user scheduling policy values.
setpriority.mechanism: The selector dispatch finds and references target processes/groups, applies `donice` or specialized background/role handlers, and checks permissions; supported selectors extend beyond a single nice integer.

getpriority.purpose: Change or query selected process/group/user scheduling policy values.
getpriority.mechanism: The selector dispatch finds and references target processes/groups, applies `donice` or specialized background/role handlers, and checks permissions; supported selectors extend beyond a single nice integer.

getrusage.purpose: Read process/children/thread resource usage according to the selector.
getrusage.mechanism: Collects accounting through `calcru` and protected proc/thread state, converts to the caller's 32/64-bit rusage ABI and copies it out.

getrlimit.purpose: Read a process resource limit pair.
getrlimit.mechanism: Uses `proc_limitget` for the selected resource and copies the current/maximum limits out.

setrlimit.purpose: Change a process resource limit pair.
setrlimit.mechanism: Copies user limits into kernel storage and calls `dosetrlimit`, which enforces privilege/resource constraints and updates associated process limits.

iopolicysys.purpose: Query or change process/thread I/O policies through a typed operation buffer.
iopolicysys.mechanism: Imports the policy request, applies MAC checks and selects disk or VFS policy helpers, including materialization/atime/permission-related policy types; each selector has its own supported scope.

process_policy.purpose: Apply or query selected process/thread resource and lifecycle policies.
process_policy.mechanism: Looks up and authorizes the target, then dispatches low-resource, CPU-use, application-lifecycle/type and related policy handlers; cleanup releases target credentials/process references.

proc_rlimit_control.purpose: Control extended process resource monitors beyond setrlimit's array.
proc_rlimit_control.mechanism: Authorizes the target and dispatches selected monitor operations, including task CPU-usage monitoring; the payload/control ABI is selector-specific.

proc_info.purpose: Query/control process information through call/flavor selectors, optionally enforcing extended identity.
proc_info.mechanism: `proc_info_internal` routes PID, fd, region, list and other operation families, checks access and copies flavor-specific data. Extended identity helps reject stale PID selection; this catalog does not enumerate every proc flavor layout.

proc_info_extended_id.purpose: Query/control process information through call/flavor selectors, optionally enforcing extended identity.
proc_info_extended_id.mechanism: `proc_info_internal` routes PID, fd, region, list and other operation families, checks access and copies flavor-specific data. Extended identity helps reject stale PID selection; this catalog does not enumerate every proc flavor layout.

proc_uuid_policy.purpose: Manage policy entries associated with executable UUIDs.
proc_uuid_policy.mechanism: Checks privilege and command inputs, copies the UUID and invokes `proc_uuid_policy_kernel`; policies are stored/queried by UUID rather than attached solely to the calling fd.

pid_suspend.purpose: Suspend or resume a selected process task under process-access policy.
pid_suspend.mechanism: Checks POSIX/MAC/entitlement and possible task-access-port authorization, references the task, then invokes pid-suspend/resume machinery; socket resumption is separately coordinated.

pid_resume.purpose: Suspend or resume a selected process task under process-access policy.
pid_resume.mechanism: Checks POSIX/MAC/entitlement and possible task-access-port authorization, references the task, then invokes pid-suspend/resume machinery; socket resumption is separately coordinated.

pid_hibernate.purpose: Request eligible process memory reclamation/freezing behavior.
pid_hibernate.mechanism: Applies process-access/MAC checks and selects configured anonymous-pageout or memorystatus freeze/inactivity machinery; it is not whole-system hibernation image creation.

pid_shutdown_sockets.purpose: Shut down sockets associated with selected process ownership under authorization.
pid_shutdown_sockets.mechanism: Validates target identity/access and iterates the relevant processes/socket shutdown machinery; it does not simply kill the process or close every fd.

task_inspect_for_pid.purpose: Obtain a restricted inspect/read task capability for an authorized PID.
task_inspect_for_pid.mechanism: Convert the supplied target task port, find and identify the process, check POSIX/MAC/task-access policy and create/copy out the requested task-port flavor. Neither entry promises a task-control right.

task_read_for_pid.purpose: Obtain a restricted inspect/read task capability for an authorized PID.
task_read_for_pid.mechanism: Convert the supplied target task port, find and identify the process, check POSIX/MAC/task-access policy and create/copy out the requested task-port flavor. Neither entry promises a task-control right.

coalition.purpose: Create, request termination of or reap a coalition.
coalition.mechanism: Validates operation/type and privileged-coalition policy, then dispatches `coalition_create_syscall`, reap or terminate helpers; requesting termination and releasing all members are different stages.

coalition_info.purpose: Read or update selected coalition information.
coalition_info.mechanism: Copies the coalition ID, obtains a referenced coalition and dispatches resource usage, name, efficiency, PID-list or debug operations; releases the reference after output handling.

coalition_ledger.mechanism: Requires privilege, imports the coalition identity and dispatches ledger operations such as the logical-write limit, then drops the coalition reference.

sys_coalition_policy_set.purpose: Set or query coalition policy such as suppression.
sys_coalition_policy_set.mechanism: Checks the entitlement and coalition type, finds a referenced coalition and invokes the flavor-specific policy set/get helper before releasing it.

sys_coalition_policy_get.purpose: Set or query coalition policy such as suppression.
sys_coalition_policy_get.mechanism: Checks the entitlement and coalition type, finds a referenced coalition and invokes the flavor-specific policy set/get helper before releasing it.

system_override.purpose: Apply a bounded privileged override of selected system resource behavior.
system_override.mechanism: Checks privilege and serializes begin/abort/end operations under the override mutex; the syscall can wait for its requested duration and then withdraw the override.

sfi_ctl.purpose: Set/query system forced-idle windows or class off-times.
sfi_ctl.mechanism: Privilege checks precede window/class selector dispatch to SFI setters/getters; query results are copied out and cancel operations remove scheduled constraints.

sfi_pidctl.purpose: Set/query a process's managed forced-idle policy.
sfi_pidctl.mechanism: Finds/iterates authorized target processes, applies `proc_apply_sfi_managed` or queries task policy, and releases target references.

usrctl.mechanism: Dispatches the requested command to `usrctl_full` or `usrctl_logout`; each path coordinates its own process/service shutdown protocol rather than executing a machine reset directly.

reboot.purpose: Request reboot, halt or other shutdown behavior selected by flags.
reboot.mechanism: Checks privilege/MAC policy, imports an optional bounded message, marks shutdown state and calls `reboot_kernel`; hardware/platform shutdown behavior is beyond this frontend.

sys_crossarch_trap.purpose: Retain a cross-architecture namespace entry point.
sys_crossarch_trap.mechanism: The body checks the namespace against `CROSSARCH_MAX_VALID_NAMESPACE`, returning `EINVAL` if invalid and `ENOTSUP` otherwise; it performs no cross-architecture execution in this source.

kill.purpose: Send a signal to a selected process or process group.
kill.mechanism: Finds/refers to the target, applies `cansignal`, and calls `psignal` or `killpg1`; posting selects pending/action state and is separate from building a user signal frame.

sigaction.purpose: Query or replace a process signal disposition.
sigaction.mechanism: Imports/converts the caller ABI, validates signal/restriction flags, copies old state out and updates handler/mask/action state used by posting and delivery.

sigprocmask.purpose: Change the calling thread's blocked-signal mask and optionally return the previous mask.
sigprocmask.mechanism: Imports the mask, uses block/unblock/set helpers, requests an AST when newly deliverable work appears, and copies old mask state out.

sigpending.purpose: Read the calling thread's pending-signal set.
sigpending.mechanism: Copies the maintained uthread pending-signal mask to the supplied user address; it does not deliver or consume those signals.

sigaltstack.purpose: Query or change the calling thread's alternate signal-stack configuration.
sigaltstack.mechanism: Converts 32/64-bit stack descriptors, validates current/on-stack restrictions and updates uthread state used by later signal delivery.

sigsuspend.purpose: Temporarily replace the signal mask and sleep for signal handling.
sigsuspend.mechanism: The nocancel body records restoration state and enters interruptible `tsleep0`; signal delivery/return restores the appropriate mask. The ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

sigsuspend_nocancel.purpose: Temporarily replace the signal mask and sleep for signal handling.
sigsuspend_nocancel.mechanism: The nocancel body records restoration state and enters interruptible `tsleep0`; signal delivery/return restores the appropriate mask. The ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

sigreturn.purpose: Restore user execution and signal-mask/alternate-stack state after a handler.
sigreturn.mechanism: Architecture-specific ARM and x86 bodies import the user context, validate tokens/machine state and install the saved state, using `EJUSTRETURN` so normal syscall result encoding does not overwrite it. Failure ordering is not an all-or-nothing memory transaction.

__pthread_kill.purpose: Send a signal to a pthread identified by a Mach thread port name.
__pthread_kill.mechanism: Converts the port to a referenced thread, checks pthread/task association and posts through `psignal_uthread`, then drops the thread reference.

__pthread_sigmask.purpose: Change/query the current pthread's signal mask.
__pthread_sigmask.mechanism: Operates on uthread mask state after user copyin, requests a signal AST as appropriate and copies the previous mask out; it bypasses process-wide disposition changes.

__sigwait.purpose: Synchronously wait for and consume a signal from a supplied set.
__sigwait.mechanism: The common body coordinates process signal state, waits when no matching pending bit exists and copies the selected signal number out. The ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

__sigwait_nocancel.purpose: Synchronously wait for and consume a signal from a supplied set.
__sigwait_nocancel.mechanism: The common body coordinates process signal state, waits when no matching pending bit exists and copies the selected signal number out. The ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

__disable_threadsignal.purpose: Mark the current thread as excluded from ordinary process-directed signal selection.
__disable_threadsignal.mechanism: Sets `UT_NO_SIGMASK | UT_CANCELDISABLE` in the current uthread, excluding ordinary signal selection and disabling cancellation handling. It does not alter every process signal disposition or the hardware interrupt mask.

__pthread_markcancel.purpose: Mark a target pthread as having cancellation pending.
__pthread_markcancel.mechanism: Converts and checks the thread port, updates uthread cancellation flags and calls `thread_abort_safely` when the current cancellation state permits interruption, then releases the thread reference.

__pthread_canceled.purpose: Query or modify the current pthread's kernel cancellation bookkeeping.
__pthread_canceled.mechanism: Dispatches actions over uthread flags/state used by cancellation-point checks; userspace pthread cleanup handlers are not implemented by this syscall body.

__semwait_signal.purpose: Wait on a Mach semaphore, optionally signaling another and applying a timeout.
__semwait_signal.mechanism: The common body converts timeout form and selects semaphore wait/timed-wait or wait-signal trap helpers; the ordinary wrapper performs its cancellation-point test.

__semwait_signal_nocancel.purpose: Wait on a Mach semaphore, optionally signaling another and applying a timeout.
__semwait_signal_nocancel.mechanism: The common body converts timeout form and selects semaphore wait/timed-wait or wait-signal trap helpers; the ordinary wrapper performs its cancellation-point test.

terminate_with_payload.purpose: Terminate an authorized target process with a structured reason/payload.
terminate_with_payload.mechanism: `terminate_with_payload_internal` validates and constructs reason state, checks the target and posts the fatal termination action; userspace strings/data are copied rather than retained as raw user pointers.

abort_with_payload.purpose: Abort the caller with a structured termination reason.
abort_with_payload.mechanism: `abort_with_payload_internal` constructs the reason object and follows fatal exit/notification behavior for the current process.

os_fault_with_payload.purpose: Report a structured process fault through the reason/payload interface.
os_fault_with_payload.mechanism: Calls `abort_with_payload_internal` with `OS_REASON_IFLAG_USER_FAULT`, enabling throttling and a user-fault branch. Security soft traps send an analytics event; other namespaces construct a user guard exception and invoke `task_violated_guard`, then free the reason and translate its result. This differs from the abort entry's `SIGABRT` delivery.

select.purpose: Wait for descriptor readability/writability/exception conditions using fd bitsets and a timeval deadline.
select.mechanism: The common body imports/converts the timeout and calls `select_internal`, which coordinates readiness scans and waits; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation before entering it.

select_nocancel.purpose: Wait for descriptor readability/writability/exception conditions using fd bitsets and a timeval deadline.
select_nocancel.mechanism: The common body imports/converts the timeout and calls `select_internal`, which coordinates readiness scans and waits; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation before entering it.

pselect.purpose: Wait for descriptor readiness with a timespec timeout and temporary signal-mask semantics.
pselect.mechanism: Imports/validates timeout and mask state, then uses `select_internal` with uthread signal coordination; the ordinary wrapper first tests cancellation.

pselect_nocancel.purpose: Wait for descriptor readiness with a timespec timeout and temporary signal-mask semantics.
pselect_nocancel.mechanism: Imports/validates timeout and mask state, then uses `select_internal` with uthread signal coordination; the ordinary wrapper first tests cancellation.

poll.purpose: Wait for readiness of an array of descriptor/event requests.
poll.mechanism: The common body builds a temporary kqueue, registers per-fd interests, scans/waits, and copies revents out, releasing temporary knotes/queue storage; ordinary poll first tests cancellation.

poll_nocancel.purpose: Wait for readiness of an array of descriptor/event requests.
poll_nocancel.mechanism: The common body builds a temporary kqueue, registers per-fd interests, scans/waits, and copies revents out, releasing temporary knotes/queue storage; ordinary poll first tests cancellation.

kqueue.purpose: Create a file-descriptor-backed event queue, optionally guarded.
kqueue.mechanism: Both call `kqueue_internal`; the guarded entry imports guard identity/restrictions before allocation/publication. The resulting fd owns queue state until close and knote teardown complete.

guarded_kqueue_np.purpose: Create a file-descriptor-backed event queue, optionally guarded.
guarded_kqueue_np.mechanism: Both call `kqueue_internal`; the guarded entry imports guard identity/restrictions before allocation/publication. The resulting fd owns queue state until close and knote teardown complete.

kevent.purpose: Apply changes and retrieve events using the legacy or fixed-width kevent ABI.
kevent.mechanism: `kevent_legacy_internal` imports change records, registers/modifies knotes and scans for output according to the selected record layout and timeout; event processing can mutate state before output copy succeeds.

kevent64.purpose: Apply changes and retrieve events using the legacy or fixed-width kevent ABI.
kevent64.mechanism: `kevent_legacy_internal` imports change records, registers/modifies knotes and scans for output according to the selected record layout and timeout; event processing can mutate state before output copy succeeds.
