kevent_qos.purpose: Apply/retrieve modern QoS-aware events for fd/workqueue-backed queues.
kevent_qos.mechanism: Adjusts caller flags, imports output-data sizing, selects `kevent_get_kqwq` or `kevent_get_kqfile`, and invokes `kevent_modern_internal` for registration and delivery.

kevent_id.purpose: Operate a dynamic workloop identified by a 64-bit ID.
kevent_id.mechanism: Gets/creates and retains the workloop, selects supported flags and enters `kevent_modern_internal`; the ID is a name for a reference-managed object, not permanent ownership.

kqueue_workloop_ctl.purpose: Create/destroy or configure workloop attributes through a control request.
kqueue_workloop_ctl.mechanism: Copies the size-bounded request and calls `kqueue_workloop_ctl_internal`; command/options determine which workloop policy or lifecycle operation is permitted.

bsdthread_create.purpose: Request creation of a pthread using registered start/stack/thread parameters.
bsdthread_create.mechanism: The local shim forwards individual arguments to `pthread_functions->bsdthread_create`; the registered pthread provider supplies the creation implementation beyond this interface.

bsdthread_register.purpose: Register pthread and workqueue user-entry information with the kernel pthread provider.
bsdthread_register.mechanism: Converts user function pointers, checks provider version and calls `bsdthread_register2` or the older callback with the appropriate stack/TSD/dispatch offsets. Provider internals are external to this shim.

bsdthread_terminate.purpose: Terminate the current pthread and coordinate stack/join notification cleanup.
bsdthread_terminate.mechanism: Locally removes workqueue membership or rejects AIO-worker termination, distinguishes a join ulock from a semaphore, records delayed port/ulock cleanup, then calls the provider's termination callback.

thread_selfid.purpose: Return the current thread's numeric ID through the pthread provider interface.
thread_selfid.mechanism: The local shim invokes `pthread_functions->thread_selfid` and passes the 64-bit result pointer; it does not return a Mach thread port right.

workq_open.purpose: Initialize a process workqueue if necessary.
workq_open.mechanism: Serializes workqueue publication, allocates state, establishes QoS/parallelism and turnstile/request machinery, and makes the queue available to subsequent worker-demand operations.

workq_kernreturn.purpose: Submit worker requests or return/park a workqueue thread through an operation selector.
workq_kernreturn.mechanism: Dispatches requests to `workq_reqthreads`, thread return, stack/event and related handlers while coordinating queue locks, thread tags and admission state; not every operation returns through the original user stack.

bsdthread_ctl.purpose: Control pthread/workqueue QoS overrides, self properties and related servicing policy.
bsdthread_ctl.mechanism: Operation dispatch selects explicit/dispatch override helpers, self-policy updates, parallelism queries, worker kill permission and supported apply/signal-mask controls with argument validation.

psynch_mutexwait.purpose: Enter the pthread provider's mutex-wait slow path with lock-generation and owner information.
psynch_mutexwait.mechanism: The shim forwards mutex address, generation values, thread identity and flags to `pthread_functions->psynch_mutexwait`; queue and priority-inheritance algorithms are not implemented in this shim.

psynch_mutexdrop.purpose: Release/wake through the pthread provider's mutex slow path.
psynch_mutexdrop.mechanism: Forwards the mutex address, generation/owner fields and flags to `pthread_functions->psynch_mutexdrop`; the returned generation/result comes from that provider.

psynch_cvbroad.purpose: Broadcast a pthread condition variable using generation/prepost state.
psynch_cvbroad.mechanism: The shim passes CV generations, associated mutex fields and thread identity to the registered `psynch_cvbroad` callback; userspace condition-variable state is coordinated by that external provider.

psynch_cvsignal.purpose: Signal a pthread condition variable, optionally selecting a thread.
psynch_cvsignal.mechanism: Forwards CV/mutex generations, target thread-port field and flags to `pthread_functions->psynch_cvsignal`; it is not a BSD signal-posting operation.

psynch_cvwait.purpose: Wait on a pthread condition variable with mutex/generation and timeout state.
psynch_cvwait.mechanism: The local shim forwards CV/mutex generations, flags and seconds/nanoseconds to the provider callback; atomic mutex-release/wait semantics must be established in the provider implementation.

psynch_cvclrprepost.purpose: Clear pthread condition-variable prepost bookkeeping through the provider.
psynch_cvclrprepost.mechanism: Forwards CV generations, prepost count/sequence and flags to `pthread_functions->psynch_cvclrprepost`; this local body adds no independent wait-queue algorithm.

psynch_rw_longrdlock.purpose: Enter the selected pthread reader/writer-lock slow-path operation.
psynch_rw_longrdlock.mechanism: Each shim invokes its correspondingly named `pthread_functions` callback with rwlock address, lock/unlock generation, writer count and flags; provider code owns the actual wait/grant protocol.

psynch_rw_rdlock.purpose: Enter the selected pthread reader/writer-lock slow-path operation.
psynch_rw_rdlock.mechanism: Each shim invokes its correspondingly named `pthread_functions` callback with rwlock address, lock/unlock generation, writer count and flags; provider code owns the actual wait/grant protocol.

psynch_rw_wrlock.purpose: Enter the selected pthread reader/writer-lock slow-path operation.
psynch_rw_wrlock.mechanism: Each shim invokes its correspondingly named `pthread_functions` callback with rwlock address, lock/unlock generation, writer count and flags; provider code owns the actual wait/grant protocol.

psynch_rw_yieldwrlock.purpose: Enter the selected pthread reader/writer-lock slow-path operation.
psynch_rw_yieldwrlock.mechanism: Each shim invokes its correspondingly named `pthread_functions` callback with rwlock address, lock/unlock generation, writer count and flags; provider code owns the actual wait/grant protocol.

psynch_rw_unlock.purpose: Release a pthread rwlock through its registered provider.
psynch_rw_unlock.mechanism: Forwards the rwlock address, generation/count and flags to `pthread_functions->psynch_rw_unlock`, returning that provider's result.

psynch_rw_unlock2.purpose: Retain an unsupported historical rwlock entry point.
psynch_rw_unlock2.mechanism: The local body returns `ENOTSUP` without invoking a provider callback.

psynch_rw_upgrade.purpose: Retain historical rwlock upgrade/downgrade entry points as no-ops.
psynch_rw_upgrade.mechanism: Both local bodies return zero and ignore their arguments. No lock conversion or provider callback occurs in these implementations.

psynch_rw_downgrade.purpose: Retain historical rwlock upgrade/downgrade entry points as no-ops.
psynch_rw_downgrade.mechanism: Both local bodies return zero and ignore their arguments. No lock conversion or provider callback occurs in these implementations.

sys_ulock_wait.purpose: Wait on a user-address lock using the older timeout ABI.
sys_ulock_wait.mechanism: Builds the extended wait arguments and calls `sys_ulock_wait2`, preserving operation/value semantics while translating the older timeout representation.

sys_ulock_wait2.purpose: Wait while a supported user lock/value condition holds, optionally using owner donation and an extended timeout/value.
sys_ulock_wait2.mechanism: Validates operation/address/value, performs atomic user reads, obtains keyed ulock state and prepares turnstile/wait state before blocking; changed values, timeout, cancellation and owner-resolution failure take explicit cleanup paths.

sys_ulock_wake.purpose: Wake one or more waiters on a keyed user-address lock.
sys_ulock_wake.mechanism: Validates operation/debug modes and calls `ulock_wake` for the process/task address key, coordinating the matching wait queue and any owner/turnstile update.

mach_eventlink_signal.purpose: Signal a Mach eventlink endpoint through the BSD syscall namespace.
mach_eventlink_signal.mechanism: Calls `mach_eventlink_signal_trap` and puts its packed 64-bit result into the BSD return-value slot while the wrapper itself returns errno zero; inner status is not a BSD errno conversion.

mach_eventlink_wait_until.purpose: Wait for an eventlink count with explicit clock/deadline/options.
mach_eventlink_wait_until.mechanism: Invokes `mach_eventlink_wait_until_trap` and returns its packed 64-bit value with outer BSD success, preserving the eventlink result contract.

mach_eventlink_signal_wait_until.purpose: Signal an eventlink and wait for the paired count/deadline operation.
mach_eventlink_signal_wait_until.mechanism: Passes both counts plus options/clock/deadline to the combined trap helper; the helper's packed result is the 64-bit syscall value, not the wrapper errno.

work_interval_ctl.purpose: Create, join/name/configure, notify or destroy a work interval through an operation selector.
work_interval_ctl.mechanism: Imports command-specific arguments and calls `kern_work_interval_*` helpers, using work-interval IDs or Mach ports according to the operation; privileges and output cleanup are command-specific.

aio_read.purpose: Enqueue an asynchronous read, write or synchronization request using a user aiocb identity.
aio_read.mechanism: `aio_queue_async_request` copies/validates request state, registers completion policy and queues owned kernel work; execution/completion and later result consumption occur separately.

aio_write.purpose: Enqueue an asynchronous read, write or synchronization request using a user aiocb identity.
aio_write.mechanism: `aio_queue_async_request` copies/validates request state, registers completion policy and queues owned kernel work; execution/completion and later result consumption occur separately.

aio_fsync.purpose: Enqueue an asynchronous read, write or synchronization request using a user aiocb identity.
aio_fsync.mechanism: `aio_queue_async_request` copies/validates request state, registers completion policy and queues owned kernel work; execution/completion and later result consumption occur separately.

aio_error.purpose: Query the completion/error state of an asynchronous request.
aio_error.mechanism: Searches the process's protected AIO state by aiocb identity and reports its maintained error/in-progress status; it does not consume the completed request.

aio_return.purpose: Consume the result of a completed asynchronous request.
aio_return.mechanism: Finds the completed entry under the AIO process lock, removes it from the done list and drops its final result ownership with `aio_entry_unref` after extracting the result.

aio_cancel.purpose: Attempt to cancel eligible queued asynchronous work for a descriptor/request.
aio_cancel.mechanism: Validates the file/request and races protected queue removal against worker admission; already running/completed requests produce different cancellation statuses and are not unconditionally aborted.

aio_suspend.purpose: Wait for completion among a list of asynchronous requests, optionally with a timeout.
aio_suspend.mechanism: The common body copies the aiocb-pointer list, searches protected AIO state and installs a bounded wait; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation first.

aio_suspend_nocancel.purpose: Wait for completion among a list of asynchronous requests, optionally with a timeout.
aio_suspend_nocancel.mechanism: The common body copies the aiocb-pointer list, searches protected AIO state and installs a bounded wait; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation first.

lio_listio.purpose: Submit a list of asynchronous I/O requests with wait/notification policy.
lio_listio.mechanism: Imports the list and optional sigevent, creates entries, registers kevents and enqueues eligible work under AIO protection; partial preparation/enqueue failures require per-entry cleanup rather than assuming one atomic batch.

semsys.purpose: Dispatch the historical SysV semaphore multiplexor.
semsys.mechanism: Bounds-checks `which` against `semcalls` and calls the selected handler with the packed trailing arguments; individual semctl/semget/semop handlers own locking and validation.

msgsys.purpose: Dispatch the historical SysV message-queue multiplexor.
msgsys.mechanism: Bounds-checks `which` against `msgcalls`, then invokes the selected message operation with packed trailing arguments; invalid selectors return `EINVAL`.

shmsys.purpose: Dispatch the historical SysV shared-memory multiplexor.
shmsys.mechanism: Bounds-checks `which` against `shmcalls` and invokes the attachment/control/detachment/get handler; the selected operation performs its own locking.

semctl.purpose: Control a SysV semaphore set, including metadata, values and removal.
semctl.mechanism: Under SysV semaphore protection, validates ID/sequence and IPC/MAC permission, then executes the command; removal also clears relevant undo state and wakes affected waiters.

semget.purpose: Find or allocate a SysV semaphore set by key.
semget.mechanism: Looks up existing identifiers/permissions or grows and initializes set/semaphore storage under subsystem protection, returning an ID with sequence identity.

semop.purpose: Apply a vector of SysV semaphore operations with wait and undo semantics.
semop.mechanism: Imports operation records, validates set identity/permissions, evaluates the vector under subsystem locking and blocks/retries when values disallow progress; undo bookkeeping is tied to process exit.

msgctl.purpose: Control a SysV message queue's metadata, limits or removal.
msgctl.mechanism: Validates queue index/sequence and command-specific IPC/MAC permission under the message-subsystem lock, then copies status, changes attributes or removes/wakes queue users.

msgget.purpose: Find or create a SysV message queue by key.
msgget.mechanism: Initializes the subsystem as needed, searches/authorizes an existing queue or allocates an unused slot with ownership and sequence metadata.

msgsnd.purpose: Append a typed message to a SysV queue, waiting for capacity when allowed.
msgsnd.mechanism: The common body validates queue identity/permissions, imports message segments and coordinates capacity waits/enqueue under subsystem protection; ordinary msgsnd first tests cancellation.

msgsnd_nocancel.purpose: Append a typed message to a SysV queue, waiting for capacity when allowed.
msgsnd_nocancel.mechanism: The common body validates queue identity/permissions, imports message segments and coordinates capacity waits/enqueue under subsystem protection; ordinary msgsnd first tests cancellation.

msgrcv.purpose: Receive a SysV message selected by type and flags.
msgrcv.mechanism: The common body searches the protected queue, waits when no eligible message exists, handles size/truncation policy and copies out/reclaims message storage; ordinary msgrcv first tests cancellation.

msgrcv_nocancel.purpose: Receive a SysV message selected by type and flags.
msgrcv_nocancel.mechanism: The common body searches the protected queue, waits when no eligible message exists, handles size/truncation policy and copies out/reclaims message storage; ordinary msgrcv first tests cancellation.

shmget.purpose: Find or create a SysV shared-memory segment by key and size.
shmget.mechanism: Under subsystem protection, chooses `shmget_existing` or `shmget_allocate_segment`, enforcing size/permission/ID sequence rules and creating memory backing for new segments.

shmat.purpose: Attach a SysV shared-memory segment into the calling process map.
shmat.mechanism: Validates segment ID/permission, chooses address/protection, installs the VM mapping and records per-process attachment state; failures unwind mapping/reference work.

shmdt.purpose: Detach a previously attached SysV shared-memory mapping.
shmdt.mechanism: Finds the caller's matching attachment, applies MAC checks and calls `shm_delete_mapping`, updating attachment counts and any pending segment-deletion lifetime.

shmctl.purpose: Control SysV shared-memory metadata, permissions or removal.
shmctl.mechanism: Validates segment identity and command authorization under subsystem protection, converts the user ABI and changes/query state; removal can defer backing destruction until attachments disappear.

shm_open.purpose: Open or create a named POSIX shared-memory object as a descriptor.
shm_open.mechanism: Imports the name, reserves fileproc state, searches/publishes a protected namespace entry and assigns typed descriptor operations; truncation and mapping later manage memory-entry-backed storage.

shm_unlink.purpose: Remove a POSIX shared-memory name from its namespace.
shm_unlink.mechanism: Looks up the name under the SHM lock, checks access/MAC and calls `pshm_unlink_internal`; existing descriptors/mappings can keep object storage alive after the name disappears.

sem_open.purpose: Open or create a named POSIX semaphore.
sem_open.mechanism: Imports/normalizes the name and team namespace, reserves descriptor state, creates a Mach semaphore when needed and publishes/reuses the protected POSIX object with ownership checks.

sem_close.mechanism: Checks descriptor type under the fd lock and calls `fp_close_and_unlock`; namespace unlink and last backing-semaphore reference are separate events.

sem_unlink.purpose: Remove a POSIX semaphore name from the protected namespace.
sem_unlink.mechanism: Uses the team/name key, checks access/MAC and calls `psem_unlink_internal`; open descriptors retain their object references.

sem_wait.purpose: Wait for a POSIX semaphore count.
sem_wait.mechanism: The common body pins a typed descriptor, checks object/MAC state and calls Mach `semaphore_wait`, translating its result before dropping the fileproc. Ordinary sem_wait tests cancellation.

sem_wait_nocancel.purpose: Wait for a POSIX semaphore count.
sem_wait_nocancel.mechanism: The common body pins a typed descriptor, checks object/MAC state and calls Mach `semaphore_wait`, translating its result before dropping the fileproc. Ordinary sem_wait tests cancellation.

sem_trywait.purpose: Attempt a POSIX semaphore decrement without waiting.
sem_trywait.mechanism: Pins/checks the typed semaphore object and calls `semaphore_timedwait` with the immediate timeout policy, translating failure/status and releasing the fd reference.

sem_post.mechanism: Pins/checks the typed object and invokes Mach `semaphore_signal`, then translates status and drops the fileproc reference.

socket.purpose: Create a protocol socket descriptor, with delegated process identity in the delegated form.
socket.mechanism: `socket_common` selects domain/type/protocol, applies policy and allocates/publishes fileproc/socket state. The ordinary entry uses the caller PID; delegation has additional identity/authorization semantics.

socket_delegate.purpose: Create a protocol socket descriptor, with delegated process identity in the delegated form.
socket_delegate.mechanism: `socket_common` selects domain/type/protocol, applies policy and allocates/publishes fileproc/socket state. The ordinary entry uses the caller PID; delegation has additional identity/authorization semantics.

socketpair.purpose: Create two connected local socket endpoints and return their descriptors.
socketpair.mechanism: Creates both sockets/fileprocs, connects them with `soconnect2`, copies descriptor numbers out and publishes reserved slots; failures close/free partial endpoints.

bind.purpose: Associate a socket with a local protocol address.
bind.mechanism: Pins the socket descriptor, imports the sockaddr, applies MAC checks and invokes `sobindlock`, then releases address and fileproc ownership.

listen.purpose: Put a socket into listening mode with an accept-backlog request.
listen.mechanism: Pins the socket, applies MAC listen checks and calls `solisten`; the protocol and socket layer manage listener state and queue limits.

accept.purpose: Remove a completed connection from a listener and create a new descriptor.
accept.mechanism: The common body checks the listener, waits/scans its accept queue, allocates accepted-socket file state and copies peer address data out; the ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

accept_nocancel.purpose: Remove a completed connection from a listener and create a new descriptor.
accept_nocancel.mechanism: The common body checks the listener, waits/scans its accept queue, allocates accepted-socket file state and copies peer address data out; the ordinary entry first tests cancellation.

connect.purpose: Connect a socket to a protocol peer.
connect.mechanism: The common body imports the sockaddr and calls `connectit`, coordinating socket state and blocking/nonblocking completion; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

connect_nocancel.purpose: Connect a socket to a protocol peer.
connect_nocancel.mechanism: The common body imports the sockaddr and calls `connectit`, coordinating socket state and blocking/nonblocking completion; the ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

connectx.purpose: Connect using extended endpoint/association and optional initial-data arguments.
connectx.mechanism: The wrapper tests cancellation then enters `connectx_nocancel`, which imports endpoints/iovecs and selects the protocol's extended connect operation with its association/connection IDs.

disconnectx.purpose: Disconnect a selected extended socket connection.
disconnectx.mechanism: Tests cancellation and calls `disconnectx_nocancel`, which resolves the socket and delegates the specified association/connection to protocol disconnect handling.

peeloff.purpose: Retain the declared peeloff interface as a local no-op.
peeloff.mechanism: The body performs an unofficial cancellation-point test and returns zero without splitting a socket association or allocating a new descriptor.

getpeername.purpose: Read the peer or local socket address.
getpeername.mechanism: Pins/locks the socket, asks the socket-filter/protocol name path for a sockaddr, copies the size-limited address and length out, then releases address storage and the file reference.

getsockname.purpose: Read the peer or local socket address.
getsockname.mechanism: Pins/locks the socket, asks the socket-filter/protocol name path for a sockaddr, copies the size-limited address and length out, then releases address storage and the file reference.

setsockopt.mechanism: Validates option length and descriptor access, applies MAC checks and calls `sosetoptlock` with a user sockopt descriptor; SOL_SOCKET and protocol levels have separate option handlers.

getsockopt.mechanism: Imports the requested size, applies MAC policy and calls `sogetoptlock`, then copies the resulting size and any option bytes out. This catalog scopes the multiplexor rather than all protocol options.

shutdown.purpose: Disable the selected send/receive direction of a socket.
shutdown.mechanism: Pins the socket and calls `soshutdown`; half-close changes socket/protocol state while the descriptor and opposite direction may remain live.

sendto.purpose: Send bytes to an optional destination through a socket.
sendto.mechanism: The common body builds a user `uio`, pins the socket and calls `sendit`, which handles address/control/policy and protocol send ownership; ordinary sendto tests cancellation.

sendto_nocancel.purpose: Send bytes to an optional destination through a socket.
sendto_nocancel.mechanism: The common body builds a user `uio`, pins the socket and calls `sendit`, which handles address/control/policy and protocol send ownership; ordinary sendto tests cancellation.

sendmsg.purpose: Send iovec data and ancillary control information through a socket.
sendmsg.mechanism: Imports the caller's msghdr/iovec ABI into a `uio`, obtains the socket and invokes `sendit`; control data may carry references. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

sendmsg_nocancel.purpose: Send iovec data and ancillary control information through a socket.
sendmsg_nocancel.mechanism: Imports the caller's msghdr/iovec ABI into a `uio`, obtains the socket and invokes `sendit`; control data may carry references. The ordinary wrapper tests cancellation.

recvfrom.purpose: Receive socket bytes and optionally copy the source address out.
recvfrom.mechanism: The common body builds a user `uio` and calls `recvit`, then releases transfer state; ordinary recvfrom adds a cancellation test before the receive path.

recvfrom_nocancel.purpose: Receive socket bytes and optionally copy the source address out.
recvfrom_nocancel.mechanism: The common body builds a user `uio` and calls `recvit`, then releases transfer state; ordinary recvfrom adds a cancellation test before the receive path.

recvmsg.purpose: Receive socket data, source address and ancillary information.
recvmsg.mechanism: Imports msghdr/iovecs, uses `recvit`, then copies updated message fields out; dequeue/control-right conversion and final user copyout are separate ownership stages. Ordinary recvmsg tests cancellation.

recvmsg_nocancel.purpose: Receive socket data, source address and ancillary information.
recvmsg_nocancel.mechanism: Imports msghdr/iovecs, uses `recvit`, then copies updated message fields out; dequeue/control-right conversion and final user copyout are separate ownership stages. Ordinary recvmsg tests cancellation.

sendmsg_x.purpose: Submit an array of extended message records for batched sending.
sendmsg_x.mechanism: Uses `sendit_x`/`sosend_list` where supported or imports individual records into `uio` operations, tracking completed records and freeing imported state on partial failure.

recvmsg_x.purpose: Receive an array of extended message records, including optimized datagram lists.
recvmsg_x.mechanism: Pins the socket and selects its batch or per-record path. In the optimized branch, `soreceive_m_list` dequeues the packet/address/control lists before individual message-header and iovec imports. Later import/copy failures free remaining lists at cleanup; this path shows no requeue rollback. See [receive-before-import ordering](../../../xnu/bsd/kern/uipc_syscalls.c#L2754) and [list cleanup](../../../xnu/bsd/kern/uipc_syscalls.c#L2938).

sendfile.purpose: Transfer file data to a socket, optionally surrounding it with header/trailer vectors.
sendfile.mechanism: Pins a regular-file vnode and socket, imports the caller ABI, handles header/trailer writes and streams file-backed data through the socket path while tracking partial bytes and references.

necp_match_policy.purpose: Evaluate application policy for supplied client parameters without creating a full client object.
necp_match_policy.mechanism: Copies the parameter buffer, calls `necp_application_find_policy_match_internal`, copies the result structure out and frees the temporary data.

necp_open.purpose: Create a descriptor for NECP client registration and observation.
necp_open.mechanism: Checks privilege/MAC and flags, allocates typed fd/client-list state, initializes locks/knote structures and publishes the descriptor; client/flow operations use it later.

necp_client_action.purpose: Manage NECP clients, flow registrations, results, agents and nexus requests.
necp_client_action.mechanism: Looks up a typed NECP fd, checks action-specific MAC policy and dispatches add/claim/remove/copy/flow/agent/request helpers; buffers and IDs have action-specific formats/lifetimes.

necp_session_open.purpose: Create a privileged NECP policy-management session descriptor.
necp_session_open.mechanism: Checks caller identity/privilege, allocates fileproc/session state through `necp_create_session` and publishes the fd; this is distinct from a client-observer descriptor.

necp_session_action.purpose: Manage policies in a NECP session.
necp_session_action.mechanism: Pins the session and holds its lock while dispatching add/get/delete/list/apply operations and related controls; applying policies updates evaluation state beyond merely copying a rule buffer.

netagent_trigger.purpose: Trigger a registered network agent by UUID.
netagent_trigger.mechanism: Imports/validates UUID and length, finds/locks the agent under registry protection and calls `netagent_send_trigger`; the userspace agent's response/work is external.

net_qos_guideline.purpose: Query network QoS guidance for the supplied request context.
net_qos_guideline.mechanism: Imports the parameter structure and inspects selected primary-interface properties such as expensive/constrained status to produce guidance; it does not reserve bandwidth or directly schedule a packet.

tracker_action.purpose: Manage/query the privileged network tracker registry through an action selector.
tracker_action.mechanism: Checks the required entitlement and dispatches tracker addition/dump operations with bounded user data; this is a registry/control interface rather than transport send/receive.

__nexus_open.mechanism: Validates/copies initialization, creates a guard identity and reserved fd, calls `nxctl_create`, copies result state out and then publishes the controller fileproc; failed construction unwinds the reservation.

__nexus_register.purpose: Register a provider owned by a nexus controller.
__nexus_register.mechanism: Imports provider parameters, obtains the controller descriptor and lock, calls `nxprov_create`, and copies the provider UUID out. On an error after creation, cleanup drops the descriptor, calls `nxprov_close`, then releases the extra provider reference. The close result replaces the original error, including a UUID copyout error, and can be zero. See [cleanup ordering](../../../xnu/bsd/skywalk/nexus/nexus_syscalls.c#L232).

__nexus_deregister.mechanism: Imports/checks the provider UUID, pins and locks the controller, calls `nxprov_destroy` and releases the reference; dependent object teardown follows provider lifecycle rules.

__nexus_create.purpose: Allocate a nexus instance from a registered provider.
__nexus_create.mechanism: Imports the provider UUID, pins/locks the controller and calls `nx_create`, then copies the new nexus UUID out. Cleanup drops the descriptor and extra caller reference; it does not undo successful instance creation on UUID copyout failure. Provider/global-list references retain the published instance. See [publication references](../../../xnu/bsd/skywalk/nexus/nexus.c#L1956) and [syscall cleanup](../../../xnu/bsd/skywalk/nexus/nexus_syscalls.c#L342).

__nexus_destroy.purpose: Destroy a nexus instance through its controller.
__nexus_destroy.mechanism: Imports/checks the UUID, pins/locks the controller and invokes `nx_destroy`; instance closure and final reference release can be distinct.

__nexus_get_opt.purpose: Query controller/provider/instance configuration selected by a nexus option.
__nexus_get_opt.mechanism: Builds a user sockopt, pins/locks the controller and calls `nxctl_get_opt`, then copies the returned output length and releases the descriptor reference.

__nexus_set_opt.mechanism: Pins/locks the controller and sends the user sockopt to `nxctl_set_opt`; the option handler interprets the specific UUID/port/configuration payload.

__channel_open.purpose: Create a guarded Skywalk channel descriptor bound to a nexus/port/ring selection.
__channel_open.mechanism: Imports and validates initialization/key data, reserves a guarded fd and calls `ch_open`; result copyout precedes final fd publication, with teardown on failure.

__channel_get_info.purpose: Read a channel's exported identity/layout information.
__channel_get_info.mechanism: Pins a typed channel fd, validates output sizing and copies `ch_info` under the channel lock, then drops the descriptor reference.

__channel_sync.purpose: Synchronize user and kernel ownership across selected channel rings.
__channel_sync.mechanism: Pins/locks the channel, checks active/admissible state, enters sync protection and ring serialization, runs validation/prologue/provider-sync/finalize routines and records partial progress/errors.

__channel_get_opt.mechanism: Pins/locks the typed channel and dispatches `ch_get_opt` using a bounded user sockopt; output length is copied back separately.

__channel_set_opt.mechanism: Pins/locks the channel, rejects inactive/nonpermissive adapters and invokes `ch_set_opt`; option handling is distinct from submitting packets through sync.

setitimer.purpose: Set a process interval timer and optionally return its previous state.
setitimer.mechanism: Imports/validates the selected timer, coordinates proc timing state and programs thread-call deadlines for real time or task virtual timers for execution-time modes.

getitimer.purpose: Read the current process interval-timer state.
getitimer.mechanism: Copies protected timer state, computes remaining real time against the current uptime when needed, converts the user ABI and copies it out.

gettimeofday.purpose: Read calendar time and supported optional time-related outputs.
gettimeofday.mechanism: Uses `clock_gettimeofday_and_absolute_time`, converts 32/64-bit timeval layout and copies requested time/timezone-related data; it does not advance timer state.

settimeofday.purpose: Set calendar time and optional timezone state under policy checks.
settimeofday.mechanism: Checks entitlement/privilege/MAC, imports/converts time values, calls `setthetime` and updates protected timezone state where requested.

adjtime.purpose: Request gradual clock adjustment and optionally read the previous adjustment.
adjtime.mechanism: Checks time-setting authorization, converts the timeval request, calls `kern_adjtime` and copies the old adjustment out; it is distinct from directly replacing calendar time.

ntp_adjtime.purpose: Read/change NTP clock-discipline parameters and return discipline status.
ntp_adjtime.mechanism: Imports the timex ABI, checks authorization for modifications, updates discipline state under `NTP_LOCK` and returns the selected output/status through the declared interface.

ntp_gettime.mechanism: Calls `ntp_gettime1` under the NTP lock, converts the caller's structure layout and copies it out.

__mach_bridge_remote_time.purpose: Convert a local timestamp through the platform's remote-time bridge.
__mach_bridge_remote_time.mechanism: Returns `mach_bridge_remote_time(local_timestamp)` in the 64-bit syscall result; synchronization/provider details live behind that kernel time helper.

thread_selfusage.purpose: Read the current thread's execution runtime.
thread_selfusage.mechanism: Returns `thread_get_runtime_self` through the syscall result ABI; it is a runtime aggregate, not a thread port or wall-clock timestamp.

thread_selfcounts.purpose: Read selected current-thread time/cycle/instruction/energy counters, optionally by performance level.
thread_selfcounts.mechanism: Under `CONFIG_PERVASIVE_CPI`, the switch invokes `_selfcounts` or `_selfcounts_perf_level`; unsupported kinds and the alternate no-support definition return `ENOTSUP`.

ledger.purpose: Query selected task ledger information, entries or template metadata.
ledger.mechanism: Imports the selector/target, checks process/MAC access, uses `ledger_info`, `ledger_get_task_entry_info_multiple` or `ledger_template_info`, and copies size-limited results out while releasing process/buffer ownership.

acct.purpose: Enable, replace or disable process accounting output to a file.
acct.mechanism: Checks privilege/MAC, opens the accounting vnode, serializes accounting subsystem state and arranges `acctwatch`; file ownership and later accounting writes outlive this syscall.

csops.purpose: Inspect or change process code-signing state using an operation selector; the audit-token variant additionally binds the request to a process identity.
csops.mechanism: Both reach `csops_internal`, which resolves the target process, applies operation-specific authorization, and switches among status, identity/blob retrieval, and flag-changing requests. The audit-token form rejects a null token before entering that helper. These are process signing operations, distinct from installing a vnode signature with `fcntl`.

csops_audittoken.purpose: Inspect or change process code-signing state using an operation selector; the audit-token variant additionally binds the request to a process identity.
csops_audittoken.mechanism: Both reach `csops_internal`, which resolves the target process, applies operation-specific authorization, and switches among status, identity/blob retrieval, and flag-changing requests. The audit-token form rejects a null token before entering that helper. These are process signing operations, distinct from installing a vnode signature with `fcntl`.

audit.purpose: Submit a userspace BSM audit record for inclusion with a kernel audit record.
audit.mechanism: The handler checks privilege or the audit-user entitlement, bounds and imports the record, validates it, and normally splices in an identity token. It attaches the resulting buffer to `kaudit_record.k_udata` with `AR_COMMIT_USER` and user trail/pipe selection flags; the audit completion path owns it afterward. Without `CONFIG_AUDIT`, the alternate body returns `ENOSYS`.

auditon.purpose: Read or modify selected audit subsystem controls.
auditon.mechanism: The command switch handles policy, queue limits, event/class mappings, audit condition and process/session-related requests using command-specific privilege, MAC and size checks, with `audit_mtx` protecting shared settings. This is a control-command family, not an arbitrary kernel-memory interface. The non-audit build returns `ENOSYS`.

getauid.purpose: Read the calling process's audit user ID.
getauid.mechanism: After the MAC check, the handler reads `cr_audit.as_aia_p->ai_auid` from the cached process credential and copies the scalar to userspace. The alternate `!CONFIG_AUDIT` body returns `ENOSYS`.

setauid.purpose: Change the process's audit user ID while preserving the other current session information.
setauid.mechanism: The handler imports the ID, performs MAC and superuser checks, copies the credential's session data and selection mask, requests a new session ID when necessary, and publishes through `audit_session_setaia`. Without `CONFIG_AUDIT` it returns `ENOSYS`.

getaudit_addr.purpose: Retrieve the calling process's extended audit identity and address/session information.
getaudit_addr.mechanism: The handler checks MAC policy and delegates sized export to `getaudit_addr_internal`, using the process credential's audit session and selection mask. The non-audit alternate returns `ENOSYS`.

setaudit_addr.purpose: Install extended audit identity, terminal address, mask and session information.
setaudit_addr.mechanism: The handler zero-initializes and imports a bounded structure, validates address family and session ID, checks MAC and superuser authority, then calls `audit_session_setaia`. If assigning a new session ID, it obtains the newly published credential and copies the assigned information back. Without `CONFIG_AUDIT` it returns `ENOSYS`.

auditctl.purpose: Replace the vnode used as the audit trail destination.
auditctl.mechanism: The handler requires superuser authority and, in external-control mode, the reserved entitlement; a null path is rejected. It opens and checks a regular vnode, applies MAC policy, retains the credential and hands the destination to `audit_rotate_vnode`, balancing its vnode iocount afterward. The non-audit alternate returns `ENOSYS`.

__mac_syscall.purpose: Invoke an operation implemented by a named MAC policy.
__mac_syscall.mechanism: After importing the policy name and applying `mac_proc_check_mac_syscall`, the handler searches static registrations and then the dynamically protected registry. It calls the matching `mpo_policy_syscall`; dynamic traversal is paired with `mac_policy_list_unbusy`. An absent matching callback yields `ENOPOLICY`; the policy owns its operation ABI.

__mac_get_file.purpose: Export selected MAC labels from a pathname, with the file form following the final symbolic link and the link form not following it.
__mac_get_file.mechanism: `mac_get_filelink` imports the requested label elements through `mac_do_get`, resolves the vnode with `namei`, copies its label into temporary storage, externalizes it and drops the vnode iocount and label. The callback implementations determine which label elements exist.

__mac_get_link.purpose: Export selected MAC labels from a pathname, with the file form following the final symbolic link and the link form not following it.
__mac_get_link.mechanism: `mac_get_filelink` imports the requested label elements through `mac_do_get`, resolves the vnode with `namei`, copies its label into temporary storage, externalizes it and drops the vnode iocount and label. The callback implementations determine which label elements exist.

__mac_set_file.purpose: Set MAC label elements on a pathname, following or not following the final symbolic link according to the variant.
__mac_set_file.mechanism: `mac_set_filelink` requires vnode labeling, allocates and internalizes a temporary label, resolves the vnode with the appropriate `FOLLOW`/`NOFOLLOW` flag, and invokes `vn_setlabel`. Each failure path releases the temporary label and any acquired vnode iocount.

__mac_set_link.purpose: Set MAC label elements on a pathname, following or not following the final symbolic link according to the variant.
__mac_set_link.mechanism: `mac_set_filelink` requires vnode labeling, allocates and internalizes a temporary label, resolves the vnode with the appropriate `FOLLOW`/`NOFOLLOW` flag, and invokes `vn_setlabel`. Each failure path releases the temporary label and any acquired vnode iocount.

__mac_get_proc.purpose: Export selected MAC label elements from the current credential.
__mac_get_proc.mechanism: `mac_do_get` handles the userspace label request and output buffer; its callback obtains `mac_cred_label(kauth_cred_get())` and calls `mac_cred_label_externalize`.

__mac_set_proc.purpose: Request a MAC credential-label update for the calling process.
__mac_set_proc.mechanism: `mac_do_set` imports the text; the callback allocates and internalizes a credential label, checks `mac_cred_check_label_update`, and calls `kauth_proc_label_update`. Temporary label storage is freed on both success and failure.

__mac_get_fd.purpose: Export MAC label elements from a vnode-backed descriptor.
__mac_get_fd.mechanism: The handler retains the `fileproc`, applies `mac_file_check_get`, obtains a vnode iocount, copies and externalizes its label, then balances both references. Despite a nearby historical comment, the switch implements only `DTYPE_VNODE`; socket and other descriptor kinds return `ENOSYS`.

__mac_set_fd.purpose: Set MAC label elements on a vnode-backed descriptor.
__mac_set_fd.mechanism: After `fp_lookup` and `mac_file_check_set`, the vnode branch requires labeling, internalizes a temporary label and calls `vn_setlabel` while holding a vnode iocount. Other descriptor kinds return `ENOSYS`; `fp_drop` and label cleanup balance ownership.

__mac_get_pid.purpose: Export selected credential-label elements for a process ID.
__mac_get_pid.mechanism: The `mac_do_get` callback obtains a referenced credential with `kauth_cred_proc_ref_for_pid`, returns `ESRCH` if absent, externalizes its label, and releases the credential. This reads credential labels, not arbitrary per-thread policy state.

audit_session_self.purpose: Obtain a Mach send-right name representing the calling process's audit session.
audit_session_self.mechanism: The handler references the current credential, rejects the default session, initializes the port's inherited selection mask when needed, calls `audit_session_mksend`, and copies the send right into the task IPC space. Credential cleanup is paired on exit; the non-audit body returns `ENOSYS`.

audit_session_join.purpose: Join the audit session represented by a supplied Mach send-right name.
audit_session_join.mechanism: The handler imports an `IKOT_AU_SESSIONPORT` send right through `ipc_typed_port_copyin_send` and delegates credential/session changes to `audit_session_join_internal`. Failed import returns `EINVAL` and the default session ID; the non-audit body returns `ENOSYS`.

audit_session_port.purpose: Obtain a Mach send-right name for a requested audit session ID.
audit_session_port.mechanism: The caller's own session requires no additional privilege; another session requires `PRIV_AUDIT_SESSION_PORT`. The handler references the session, creates/copies out its port and writes the name to userspace, dropping session/credential references and deallocating an already installed name if final copyout fails. Without audit support it returns `ENOSYS`.

csrctl.purpose: Query whether requested SIP/CSR permissions are allowed or retrieve the active CSR configuration.
csrctl.mechanism: The dispatcher recognizes only `CSR_SYSCALL_CHECK` and `CSR_SYSCALL_GET_ACTIVE_CONFIG`, forwarding to helpers that validate the supplied buffer and call the CSR policy functions. Unknown operations return `ENOSYS`; this entry does not provide a general configuration setter.

getentropy.purpose: Fill a userspace buffer with at most 256 bytes from the kernel random subsystem.
getentropy.mechanism: The handler rejects larger requests, fills a fixed stack buffer through `read_random`, and copies exactly the requested count out. The random generator's internal construction is beyond this syscall wrapper.

oslog_coproc_reg.purpose: Register a coprocessor firmware UUID and harvest-file path with kernel logging.
oslog_coproc_reg.mechanism: The caller must be a DriverKit task and hold the coprocessor-logging entitlement. The handler bounds and imports the path and UUID, calls `os_log_coprocessor_register_with_type` with the filesystem-table harvest type, and releases its temporary allocation.

oslog_coproc.purpose: Submit a coprocessor log payload with UUID, timestamp, format offset and streaming selection.
oslog_coproc.mechanism: The handler requires a DriverKit task plus entitlement, checks the full record size with overflow detection, imports payload and UUID, calls `os_log_coprocessor`, and frees the payload on success or failure.

gethostuuid.purpose: Retrieve the platform UUID, allowing the platform lookup to wait for the supplied timeout.
gethostuuid.mechanism: The handler applies the entitlement/platform/MAC branch, converts the process-width `timespec`, calls `IOBSDGetPlatformUUID`, then copies the UUID out. An unsuccessful IOKit lookup becomes `EWOULDBLOCK`; the entitlement is not an unconditional requirement on every configuration.

kdebug_typefilter.purpose: Map the kernel tracing type-filter bitmap read-only into the calling address space.
kdebug_typefilter.mechanism: The handler maps `kdbg_typefilter_memory_entry` with `mach_vm_map_kernel`, read-only protections and shared inheritance, copies out the resulting pointer using the map's address width, and deallocates the mapping if that copyout fails. In this body the size pointer is checked for null but not written.

kdebug_trace_string.purpose: Associate, update or terminate a string identifier in the kernel debug trace stream.
kdebug_trace_string.mechanism: Tracing and event/process filters can make the call return without recording. Otherwise it validates the debug ID and string ID, imports a bounded string (allowing truncation), and calls `kernel_debug_string_internal`; a null string with a valid existing ID takes the termination path.

kdebug_trace64.purpose: Emit a kernel debug trace event with four user-supplied arguments.
kdebug_trace64.mechanism: The narrow wrapper builds the 64-bit argument structure and delegates. `kdebug_trace64` returns immediately when tracing is disabled; otherwise it rejects kernel-only event IDs and calls `kernel_debug_internal`, supplying the current thread ID rather than a user-selected fifth argument.

kdebug_trace.purpose: Emit a kernel debug trace event with four user-supplied arguments.
kdebug_trace.mechanism: The narrow wrapper builds the 64-bit argument structure and delegates. `kdebug_trace64` returns immediately when tracing is disabled; otherwise it rejects kernel-only event IDs and calls `kernel_debug_internal`, supplying the current thread ID rather than a user-selected fifth argument.

sys_panic_with_data.purpose: Request a kernel panic carrying a bounded userspace message and auxiliary data.
sys_panic_with_data.mechanism: The handler requires the extended-panic-log entitlement, imports or substitutes message/data/UUID fields and derives debugger options from supported flags. Allocation or copy failures converge on the final `panic_with_data` call rather than an ordinary successful return.

sysctl.purpose: Read or write an individual registered system-control node, addressed by numeric OID or name.
sysctl.mechanism: The numeric form imports the OID array; the named form allocates and terminates an imported name. Both construct a `sysctl_req` with userspace copy functions and call `userland_sysctl`, which resolves the node and enforces its access policy. They export the resulting old length, including the `ENOMEM` size-reporting case. Individual OID handlers are a separate interface surface.

sys_sysctlbyname.purpose: Read or write an individual registered system-control node, addressed by numeric OID or name.
sys_sysctlbyname.mechanism: The numeric form imports the OID array; the named form allocates and terminates an imported name. Both construct a `sysctl_req` with userspace copy functions and call `userland_sysctl`, which resolves the node and enforces its access policy. They export the resulting old length, including the `ENOMEM` size-reporting case. Individual OID handlers are a separate interface surface.

telemetry.purpose: Select telemetry setup/read operations or set the current thread's voucher name.
telemetry.mechanism: Under `CONFIG_TELEMETRY`, the command switch reaches PMI, page-in and memory-usage helpers; the timer-event command returns `ENOTSUP`. The voucher-name command calls `thread_set_voucher_name` independently of that guard. Unknown or unavailable commands return `EINVAL`.

proc_trace_log.purpose: Request delivery of a particular process's trace-memory data.
proc_trace_log.mechanism: The handler checks `PRIV_PROC_TRACE_INSPECT`, finds and references the PID, verifies the supplied unique ID to reject PID reuse, calls `task_send_trace_memory`, and releases the process reference. Missing/mismatched identity yields `ENOENT`.

stack_snapshot_with_config.purpose: Collect or retrieve a stackshot using the versioned stackshot configuration ABI.
stack_snapshot_with_config.mechanism: The wrapper checks superuser authority and the configured entitlement/reporting policy, validates the version and exact structure size, imports the configuration and calls `kern_stack_snapshot_internal`. It translates Mach results through `stackshot_kern_return_to_bsd_error` and may report the authorization/outcome stage.

microstackshot.purpose: Control or retrieve the telemetry microstackshot stream.
